# Changelog

Notable changes to `association`, newest first. Each entry links back to the
commit that made it for the full story.

Released versions follow [semantic versioning](https://semver.org): the major
number changes when something that used to work stops working, the minor
number when something is added, the patch number for fixes. What counts as
"something that used to work" here is the CLI surface - command and option
names, output shapes that scripts parse - and the documented Python API, not
the set of question shapes the reader names or the wording of an answer, which
are expected to grow.

Sections dated rather than numbered predate the first release, when the project
had no published version to be compatible with.

## Unreleased
- **A count of a yes/no measure over a line keeps both: "most 30 point triple doubles in the last 3 years" was refused "'30' is a number this reading did not use ...", and now ranks "every player, regular season career (2024 on) with a triple-double and 30+ points, by player: Nikola Jokic 35 G, Luka Doncic 25 G, Giannis Antetokounmpo 12 G ..."; "how many 30 point triple doubles does jokic have" counts 57 where every triple-double (197) was counted** (ISSUES.md #437 and #394's half, closed and narrowed; ROADMAP.md, Phase 5, step 6, lane L). The count's child grammar reads "N stat triple doubles" (and double-doubles) as its games (`lexicon.CHILD_THRESHOLD_COUNT`); the league's count adds the keyed line beside a yes/no measure as a second predicate on the same game, whatever stat the words also name (`point._everyone_threshold_predicates`), and steps past the boolean game ranking for it ("most 30+ point triple doubles" listed three single games, `point._everyone_boolean_game_ranking`); a named player's count does the same (`point._move_boolean_count`). Proved against the push before: 1 of the 2,082 feed answers moved (above), 0 of the 628; the held grammar drop for it leaves `tests/grammar_drops.py` (the harness 31 -> 30 drops, 5 held by text) and its reader case's reason is rewritten; the claims ledger falls 2,795 -> 2,794 feed unread words, lowered; ratchets unchanged. #394 is narrowed to a line at 0 ("most 0 point games in nba team history", refused by name).
- **A team's box-score count given up is its opponents', summed by the team compiler: "how many assists on average do the mavericks give up" answered "The Dallas Mavericks' assists per game was 25.3 ...", their own, and now "The Dallas Mavericks' opponents had 2,325 assists against them over 82 games in the 2026 regular season (26-56), 28.4 per game."; "threes allowed by the celtics this season" and "celtics opp 3pm this season" were refused "no team metric", and now answer the opponents' 1,149** (ISSUES.md #425, its reader's remainder; ROADMAP.md, Phase 5, step 6, lane L). `lexicon.GIVEN_UP_KEYS` holds every box-score count the team compiler sums from the opponents' box rows (points, rebounds, assists, steals, blocks, turnovers, fouls, field goals, free throws, threes made), so the verb makes each the opponents' ("how many rebounds did the celtics give up" answered the Celtics' own 46.4); `point._team_measure` states the team's total over an opponents' measure as over its own (the compiler reads the typed measure's `whose`), an alias text included ("opp 3pm"); and the catalog reads "steals allowed", "blocks allowed", "turnovers forced", "fouls drawn", "field goals allowed" and "free throws allowed" as the opponents' (`measure.ALIASES`, `lexicon.MEASURE_GRAMMAR`). Proved against the commit before: 1 of the 2,082 feed answers moved (the Mavericks', above), 0 of the 628. The claims ledger falls 2,796 -> 2,795 feed unread words, lowered; ratchets, harnesses and reader cases unchanged. What is left of #425: an opponents' percentage ("celtics opponents fg% this season") and a ranking of teams by a figure given up ("which team gave up the most rebounds") are refused by name.
- **A season's first games beside a count of seasons is a window per season, refused by name: "warriors record in the first 15 games last 10 season" listed "Golden State Warriors, first 15 of 793 games (since 2017, 2017 regular season) (13-2): ..." - the range's first 15, all of 2016-17's - and now "A window of games in each season ('first 15 games' last 10 season) is read by nothing here yet - name one season for its first 15 games, or ask for the seasons whole."** (ISSUES.md #432, closed; ROADMAP.md, Phase 5, step 6, lane L). `window.per_season_window` read a window beside "each/every/per season" alone; it reads "first N games" beside "last/past N seasons" too (`lexicon.FIRST_GAMES_OF_SEASONS`), and the parser refuses it by the `window_per_season` cause, as it refuses "warriors first 10 game record every season" (#379). Proved against the push before (`e5ff0133`): 1 of the 2,082 feed answers moved (above), 0 of the 628; the ledgers, ratchets, harnesses and reader cases unchanged. A record over each season's first N games stays unread (a new shape's occasion, D11).

That is 274 in total."** (ISSUES.md #412, closed; ROADMAP.md, Phase 5, step 6, lane L). The ranking's points default stood wherever neither the words nor the model named a measure; it is the `ranking_needs_stat` cause (at the end of `CAUSES`), written by the parser's last step as a defaulted word's cause is (`parse._defaulted_ranking`, `Reading.defaulted`) and said by the planner only where the ranking would answer - so a decline, a floor or a refusal the planning comes to first keeps its sentence, and what the words name that nothing reads (an age) stays the refusal. - **A reading's cause carries the key the words ask, not the page's label: the `intent` fact of the 17 kinds of cause that carried one is a `shape` fact holding the `reading.PointShape`, and the sayer's phrase tables (`say._LINE_SHAPES`, `_STAT_FOR`, `_REACHING`, `_unknown_stat`) are keyed by it (the Phase 3 review, section 3: the label still keyed four of the sayer's tables).** A sentence that prints the retired name - a shape's decline, "Nothing here answers this question: <label>: ...", and a player named on a team's question - reads it off the key through `reading.asked_label`, and the page's data beside a cause shows it as `intent` still (`compose.plan._page_facts`); `ShapeDeclined.labeled(cause, intent)` is `ShapeDeclined.under(cause, asked)`. No answer moves: against the run before it the 628, the 2,082 and the 2,710 readings are identical, text and data, once each cause's `shape` fact is read back as the label it replaced (10, 176 and 186 cause facts), and so are the unit-test calls (134); 16 of `tests/query/reader_cases.json`'s 467 cases move in that fact alone.
- **A year and the next year's last two digits written with a space between are the season they span: "victor wembanyama 2025 26 stats" answers his 2025-26 line, where it answered 2024-25's with "26" unread (the feed's unread numbers, ISSUES.md #382).** `lexicon.SEASON_SPAN` reads "2015 16" as it reads "2015-16", only where the second number follows the first and no line or count reads it ("2025 26 points", "2024 25+" stay a year and a line). Proved against a fresh run of `8e1a787`: the 628 and the unit-test calls identical (the new cases added), 3 of the 2,082 feed answers and the same 3 of the 2,710 readings moved:
  - "lebron james stats in 2015 16": "... in 69 games in the 2015 regular season." -> "LeBron James averaged 25.3 points, 7.4 rebounds and 6.8 assists per game in 76 games in the 2016 regular season."
  - "victor wembanyama 2024 25 stats": "... in 71 games in the 2024 regular season." -> "Victor Wembanyama averaged 24.3 points, 11 rebounds and 3.7 assists per game in 46 games in the 2025 regular season."
  - "victor wembanyama 2025 26 stats": "... in 46 games in the 2025 regular season." -> "Victor Wembanyama averaged 25 points, 11.5 rebounds and 3.1 assists per game in 64 games in the 2026 regular season."

  The claims ledger: 702 on the 628, unchanged; 3,663 -> 3,660 on the 2,082, and 180 -> 177 questions with an unread number (`scripts/ledger_held.json` lowered).
- **A season written as a span and then "to" a bare year is the range between them: "how many games did miami heat play 2008-09 to 2025" reads 2009 through 2025, where the span's one season answered (the feed's unread numbers, ISSUES.md #382).** `span._validate_range_to_year` reads a span, "to" or "through", and a bare year as the range from the span's season to the season the year names (a bare year is a season number, as "since 2020" and "from 2002 to 2004" read it); a bare year before a span ("tmac 2001 to 2001-02") is still the span's season. Proved against a fresh run of `8e1a787`: the 628 and the unit-test calls identical (the new cases added), 3 of the 2,082 feed answers and the same 3 of the 2,710 readings moved:
  - "curry playoff stats 2014-15 to 2017 including ts% and efg% and turnover percentage": "Paul Pierce led the league in true shooting % in the 2015 postseason ..." -> "every player, postseason career (2015-2017), by player (TS% per game, minimum 20 games): ..." (the feed carries no model names, so "curry" is read by nothing in both).
  - "how many games did miami heat play 2008-09 to 2025": "Miami Heat, 2009 regular season (82 games): ..." -> "Nothing here answers this question: team_stat: team_stat cannot honor ['since', 'until'] - ..."
  - "kobe stats 1999-00 to 2002 with shaq": "Kobe Bryant with and without Shaquille O'Neal (Los Angeles Lakers), 2000 regular season: ..." -> "Nothing here answers this question: with_without: with_without cannot honor ['since', 'until'] - ..."

  The claims ledger: 702 on the 628, unchanged; 3,666 -> 3,663 on the 2,082, and 183 -> 180 questions with an unread number (`scripts/ledger_held.json` lowered).
- **A private-use character typed into a question forges no typed value: "nikola jokic \ue00a stats this season" answers his season line, where it answered a 10-game log (ISSUES.md #383).** The grammars read the question with each typed value written over by a mark from Unicode's Private Use Area (`lexicon.LINE_MARK_*`, `OPPONENT_MARK*`, `COMPANION_MARK*`, `WINDOW_MARK`, `DATE_MARK`: U+E000-U+E00B), and nothing stripped the range on intake, so a mark typed by hand read as a value no tagger read. The parser's first step (`parse.read_route`) reads every character of U+E000-U+F8FF as a space where it stands, in the question and the model's names (`lexicon.unmarked`, `PRIVATE_USE_FIRST`, `PRIVATE_USE_LAST`), so every claim's offset holds; a test holds every mark inside that range. No question in the four populations holds one: 628 of 628 recorded answers, 2,082 of 2,082 feed answers and 2,710 of 2,710 readings identical, the unit-test calls 3,712 of 3,712 (the 48 new cases' calls added); the claims ledger 702 on the 628 and 3,666 on the 2,082, unchanged.
- **A record over a floor of minutes with no stat line beside it is keyed on the floor: "victor wembanyama record when playing 30 or more minutes" splits his games at 30 minutes (32 games 23-9, 33 under 30 27-6), where it refused "A record in the games over a line needs the number of minutes each game has to reach, and none was read."** Once #374 read the floor, it was a line the relation narrowed by, and a record over a line keys on an "N stat" pair; under the record's key (`point.lines_under`) a lone floor kept at or over a number is the record's own line, keyed and narrowing nothing. Found while fixing #374, on a hand-written reply. No answer, reading or call moves in the four populations (none states it).
- **A count's line beside a floor or ceiling at the same number on another stat is counted and said beside it: "how many games did victor wembanyama have 30 points playing 30 or more minutes" counted his 112 games of 30+ minutes, the 30-point line dropped; it counts his 32 games with 30+ points and at least 30 minutes.** Three readings of "a phrase carrying the count's number is the count" compared the number alone: the point's predicate (`point._default_threshold_count`, a substring test of the number in the phrase's words), the count reader's said lines (`compose.counts`) - each now takes the phrase for the count only where it is on the same stat or holds the keyed line's own words ("14 fta" inside "under 14 fta", the model's stat another) - and the measure, which read the longer box-score word "minutes" over the keyed line's "points": under a count or a record the keyed line names the stat beside a phrase (`point.lines_under`). Found while fixing #374. No answer, reading or recorded question moves in the four populations (no wording in them states both); the unit-test calls identical but the re-seated test below. `test_a_line_below_a_number_counts_the_games_under_it_on_the_stat_the_words_name` reads its lines from the words, as the lines tagger reads them, where its slot door built a keyed line from a slot that no reading produces.
- **A window of games taken in each season is refused by a cause naming both, where the team log answered one season's: "warriors first 10 game record every season" answered "Golden State Warriors, first 10 games of the 2026 regular season (5-5)", "every season" unread (ISSUES.md #379).** `window.per_season_window` reads a window of games (an end of `lexicon.WINDOW_GRAMMAR`, or `ORDER_WORDS`) beside `lexicon.EACH_SEASON` ("each", "every" or "per" season or year, "season by season"); where both stand the parser's refusal before any point is `window_per_season` (`Reading.refused`, facts `window` and `per`). Nothing reads a window per season yet - the games relations cut one window from the span, and a player's history cut "his first 10 games each season" from his whole career and grouped one season - so every key refuses it; #372 (a team's "last N seasons" on the team-season relation) is the step that could read it. A bare "by season" is not read: deleting "regular" from "julius rankdle last 15 games stats vs lakers by regular season game" made one, and the refusal claimed the word. Feed answers (2,082), 1 moved, the 2,710 readings the same 1, the 628 recorded questions identical, the unit-test calls 3,703 of 3,703 aligned (`calls_aligned.py --new-kind window_per_season`):
  - "warriors first 10 game record every season": "Golden State Warriors, first 10 games of the 2026 regular season (5-5): ..." -> "A window of games in each season ('first 10 game' every season) is read by nothing here yet - name one season for its first 10 game, or ask for the seasons whole."

  The claims ledger: 702 on the 628, unchanged; 3,668 -> 3,666 on the 2,082.
- **A question naming both ends of the games at once is refused by a cause naming both: "lebron james last 5 first games stats" answered his first 10 games, "last" and "5" unread (ISSUES.md #378).** `window.contradicting_ends` reads each end the words name - with a count (`lexicon.COUNTED_END`: "last 5", "first 10", not a count of seasons) or with "games" (`ORDER_WORDS`) - and where both ends stand the parser's refusal before any point is `window_ends_contradict` (`Reading.refused`, facts `ends`: the words of each), said "The question names both ends of the games at once ('last 5' and 'first games') - ask for the first games or the last ones, not both." Neither end is right over the other, and no default of one would be correctable by a wording the question did not already hold. Feed answers (2,082), 1 moved, the 2,710 readings the same 1, the 628 recorded questions identical, the unit-test calls 3,700 of 3,700 aligned (`calls_aligned.py --new-kind window_ends_contradict`, the one `refusal_result` call the cause sentence check adds):

- **Breaking (Python API): the grammar names what the words ask as a `PointShape`, not an intent - the intent leaves the reader (Phase 3, step 4, slice (a)).** The three choosers - the parent grammar by the subject's kind (`parse.PARENT_GRAMMAR`, whose rows name a `reading.PointShape`), the child grammars (`subject._CHILD_GRAMMARS`) and the stages before the taggers (`router._settle_stages`) - name the relation, the shape and the `by` of the point the words ask for bare: one key per retired intent (`reading.PLAYER_LOG`, `PLAYER_LINE`, `PLAYER_SPLITS`, `LINE_RECORD`, `PERIOD_LOG`, `GAMES_COUNTED`, `GAME_HIGHS`, `LINE_RUNS`, `PLAYER_MEETINGS`, `PRESENCE_SPLIT`, `TEAM_MEETINGS`, `TEAM_PERIOD_TOTAL`, `PERIOD_RANKING`, `TEAM_RECORD`, `NETPOINTS_RATINGS`, `NETPOINTS_FINGERPRINT`, `SHOT_CHART`, `SHOT_DISTANCE`, `PLAYER_RANKING`, `PLAYER_COMPARISON`, `SEASON_HISTORY`, `TEAM_LINE`, `TEAM_RANKING`, `TEAM_OUTLOOK`, `TEAM_COACH`; `None` for the retired `other`), carried as `Reading.asked`, `Route.asked`, `Subject.asked` and `subject.Applied.asked`. Measured first (`~/association-research/stages/intent_family.py`, the 2,710 readings, at `a26d438`): the final intent is the parent grammar's on 2,383, a child grammar's on 275, the stages' on 52; an intent maps to up to four PLANNED keys (`player_stat`: the season line 405, the games' line 262, rows by date 15, none 1), since the relation and sometimes the shape follow the typed filters, and two planned keys are reached by more than one intent (`player_games` rows by date: `game_log` 297, `player_stat` 15; the game-level ranking: `leaderboard` 367, `game_log` 3, `other` 1) - so the key is what the words ASK, the planned `PointShape` what the point IS, and the page's label is keyed by the asked one; the subject's kind stays the subject reading's (the grammar is keyed by it, never names it). Every intent set and intent-keyed table is a set of keys or a predicate: `reading.PLAYER_ASKS`, `TEAM_ONLY_ASKS`, `PLAYER_REQUIRED_ASKS`, `SUBJECT_RESTORABLE_ASKS`, `OWN_TEAM_RESTORABLE_ASKS` (the `*_INTENTS` sets), `reading.on_a_declared_relation` over `DECLARED_RELATIONS` (where `CHART_INTENTS` stood), `router.CODE_ASSIGNED_ASKS`, `subject.KIND_ASSIGNED_ASKS`, `line.THRESHOLD_ASKS`, `period.PERIOD_ASKS`, `window.ORDER_ASKS`, `point.DEFAULT_POINTS`/`_ROWS_BY`/`_COUNT_SHAPES` keyed by the key, `point.TEAM_SEASON_POINTS` the three keys themselves (each the point's shape); the taggers' contexts take `asked=` (`SpanContext`, `WindowContext`, `CutsContext`, `PeriodContext`, `LineContext`, `MeasureContext`); `parse.parent_intent` is `parse.parent_asked`; `settle`, `read_subject`, `settle_subject`, `child_named`, `apply_subject`, `default_point`, `team_season_point` and `Reading.from_slots` take the key; `compose.COMPILED_INTENTS` is gone (every key is the compiler's: the answering loop asks `Reading.asked is not None`). `Reading.intent` (and `Subject.intent`, `Route.intent`) is the page's label alone, ONE table (`reading.SHAPE_NAMES`, moved from `compose.plan` and keyed by the asked shape as well as the planned one, the coach's `(team_seasons, scalar, coach)` added) through `reading.asked_label`, filled from the key and held to it (`reading.labeled`): `Answer.intent`, the trace, the records and a cause's `intent` fact read it, nothing decides by it. - **Breaking (Python API): the planner checks a point's typed cells against its relation's table and its shape's row, in one check, and the slot-era declarations it read are gone (Phase 3, step 2's closing slice).** `player_relation.RELATION_SCOPING_EXCLUDED` and `team_relation.TEAM_RELATION_SCOPING_EXCLUDED` are keyed by the planned point's `reading.PointShape` - one row per route in `compose._ROUTES`, 21 on the player relation and 11 on the team relation (a test holds the keys equal, beside `SHAPE_NAMES` and `coverage.SOURCES`) - where they were keyed by the retired templates' names, and each row is a new `reading.ShapeCells`: `unstated` (the cells its words do not state, each with its reason - 243 rows where 138 stood under 24 names: the 170 that carry an old row's cell keep its reason word for word, and 73 under 16 new reasons say the cells a shape's words never named: a season line's, a high's, a count's, a comparison's, the NetPoints readers', the ranking by a quarter's, the with/without split's and the team-season readers' line, companion, split, window, ranked measure and quarter), `refused` (what the planner refuses outright, saying the first one's reason: a run, a quarter's split, two players' meetings), `taken` (beyond the relation's table: the season-line ranking's unit, a team record's month, the teammate, line and ordinal season a team's log, splits and record over a line refuse in their own words, the team compiler's unit on a team's own season), `declined` (`"plan"`: the planner declines what the words do not state, where the shape's reader is the point's only answer; `"read"`: a team's own season's reader declines when asked), `sides` (one named half of the starter/bench split, never the bare category) and `named_player`/`named_subject` (a run's cells only a named player's, or a named team's or player's, games carry). `compose.plan.cells_unhonored(scope, key)` is the one check - the `(slot, cell, why)` of every cell a scope sets beyond what the shape states (`cells_stated(key)`: the table and what the row takes, less what it does not state) - read by the planner, the season line's readers' check and the answer side (`compose._read`, which steps aside, or declines in the shape's sentence, before it asks a reader); `cells_declined(point, key)` is what the planner refuses before any reader runs, keyed by the shape where `_shape_declines` branched on the reading's intent; `beyond_words` words the decline; `shape_cells(key)` finds the row. `reading.Scope.cells()` is every cell a scope sets - each family's and the split's (`Scope.CELLS` names them; the line family's alone until now) - and `reading.cell_slots(scope, cell)` the slot names a decline says each by, so every sentence is word for word. - **"76ers" is read as the team it names: "giannis stats vs 76ers this season", "Kd log vs 76ers", "76ers leaders in 3s" read the 76ers from the words.** The subject reading splits every name into its letter runs, so "76ers" - the one team name spelled with a digit - was the word "ers", and no team was read from it: the opponent after "vs" (`subject._team_after_versus`), the own team after "for" (`_team_after_for`) and the team the question is about (`team_named_in`) all missed it, and a reading that held no model span for it (the words-only feed population) answered the league or the player's whole season. `lexicon.TEAM_SINGULARS` holds "76ers" (its one-word spellings the roster split cannot find), read whole in the question's order (`lexicon.TEAM_SPELLING_RUN`; "chicago bulls vs 76ers" is still the Bulls against the 76ers), and every team the words name is one no player's name is read from (`subject._teams_by_word` - "how many times did the 76ers play boston" would otherwise have read Brandon Boston Jr. once the 76ers stood first). Measured on the four populations against `0f87652`: 2,669 of 2,710 readings identical; the 628 recorded questions 608 identical and 20 moved in the reading and the planned query alone - each a team the model's span named "76ers" now read as "Philadelphia 76ers" from the words, one ("Payton Prichard stats vs 76ers at home including playoffs game log", 3 wordings) the opponent where an unplaced team stood - every result, answer and remark identical; the 2,082 feed answers 2,061 identical, 3 moved in the reading (one with its planned query, the team spelled in full) and nothing after it ("kobe finals stats vs 76ers", "most assists in a season by a 76ers power forward in the 2000s", "Tim Hardaway jr stats vs 76ers gamelog") and 18 answers moved: 12 to the question asked - "76ers leaders in 3s" (Kon Knueppel led the league ... -> Tyrese Maxey led the Philadelphia 76ers in 3-pointers made ..., at 220), "giannis stats vs 76ers this season" (his 27.6 points ... in 36 games -> "played 36 games in the 2026 regular season, none of them vs the Philadelphia 76ers"), "Kd log vs 76ers" (his last 10 games -> his 2 games vs the 76ers), "jalen brunson last 5 home games vs 76ers" and "Kat last 5 home games vs 76ers" (their last 5 home games -> their last 5 home games vs the 76ers), "cade cunningham assists+rebounds all-time game log vs 76ers" (his last 10 games -> his 8 vs the 76ers), "most points in a game for a 76ers player" (Bam Adebayo's 83 -> Tyrese Maxey's 54, 44 and 43), "nba players from the 76ers in the 2000s" (the league's scorers -> the 76ers', Allen Iverson's 29.9), "highest scoring games of 76ers players" (the league's points leaders -> the 76ers'), "76ers versus chicago bulls spread last 10 games" ("No games for every player vs the Chicago Bulls" -> the two teams' last 10 meetings, 4-6), "chicago bulls vs 76ers spread last 10 games" and "clippers vs 76ers scores last 20" (2 wordings) (the Bulls' or the Clippers' last games -> their last meetings with the 76ers); 3 from one wrong answer to another ("brunson last 5 home games vs 76ers" and "josh hart last 5 home games vs 76ers", whose player the words alone do not read: the league's home scorers -> "No games for every player vs the Philadelphia 76ers at home"; "games with 13+ free throw attempts by the 76ers": the league's free-throw attempts -> the 76ers' 24.8 per game); and 2 to the team's season line where a single game was asked, as production already answers them from the model's span (ISSUES.md, filed with this change): "most points in a single game on the 76ers" (Tyrese Maxey's 54 -> "The Philadelphia 76ers' points per game was 115.9 ...") and "best free throw percentage in a game with 13+ free throw attempts by the 76ers" (the 76ers players' single games -> the team's 80.9%). Unit-test calls 2,650 of 2,652 identical, the 2 others a team the test's words name "76ers" now spelled as the reading reads it; the ledger 702, identical. Pinned in `tests/query/test_subject_value.py`.
- **A player's name after "vs" is no team its first word only clips: "KEVIN GARNETT VS TIM DUNCAN GAMES" is a matchup of two players, not one refused for an opponent.** The subject reading's opponent (`subject._team_after_versus`) tried the words after "vs" against the teams, three down to one, and "TIM" resolved by the start of "Timberwolves" (`entities._team_named`'s word-prefix match), so the matchup carried the Minnesota Timberwolves as its opponent and was refused "player_matchup cannot honor ['opponent'] - ... there is no third team to narrow them to". A span the team only clips - none of its words a word of the team's name, its abbreviation, a nickname or its singular - is now no team where every word of it is a name the question gives a player (`subject.players_named_in`); "vs buck" stays the Bucks, "vs the wolves" the Timberwolves. Measured on the four populations against `298f0ac`: 628 of 628 recorded questions, 2,708 of 2,710 readings and 2,652 of 2,652 unit-test calls identical; the 2 moved feed answers, each from a false-cause refusal to the matchup's own sentence: "KEVIN GARNETT VS TIM DUNCAN GAMES" ("Nothing here answers this question: player_matchup: player_matchup cannot honor ['opponent'] - two players' meetings are the games they played against each other - there is no third team to narrow them to." -> "Kevin Garnett has no games in the 2026 regular season in the warehouse.") and "SHAQ VS TIM DUNCAN GAME STATS" (the same refusal -> "Shaquille O'Neal has no games in the 2026 regular season in the warehouse."), which is the matchup's own default season for two retired players (ISSUES.md, filed with this change); the ledger 702, identical. - **A quarter is never the one who scored in it, and "most recent" is no ranking: "display the first quarter scores for the Sixers' most recent 10 games" lists the 76ers' ten first quarters.** The grammar a dropped subject is read back from (`subject.subject_named_in`, `lexicon.SUBJECT_OF_HIGH`) read "first quarter" as the name before "scores", the quarter stage made him the player and dropped the Sixers, and the answer was "No player found matching 'first quarter' - did you mean Tim Quarterman?"; and the team ranking's words (`lexicon.RANK_WORDS`) read the "most" of "most recent" as the ranking's end, so a team's quarter would have answered the highest of the ten. `lexicon.NOT_A_SUBJECT` holds the period words ("quarter", "half", "qtr", "period", "overtime", ...), and `RANK_WORDS`' "most" does not match before "recent". Measured on the four populations against the subject slice (`1d5b4ca`): 627 of 628 recorded questions identical and the one moved is this question ("No player found matching 'first quarter' - did you mean Tim Quarterman?" -> "The Philadelphia 76ers, 1st quarter scoring over their last 10 games, 2026 regular season (10 games, 293 total): 2026-03-25 38 vs Chicago Bulls, ..."); 2,709 of 2,710 readings identical, the same one moved (`period_split` for "first quarter" -> `team_quarter_points` for the 76ers); 2,082 of 2,082 feed answers and 2,650 of 2,650 unit-test calls identical; no other population question has a period word as the grammar's subject or "most recent" beside a rank; the ledger 702 unread of 2,411 content words (the question's "first quarter" is no name now, so two of its words are content words, both read). Pinned in `tests/query/test_subject_value.py`.
- **Breaking (Python API): who a question is about is one typed value written by one reader, and the four name slots and the point's position that carried it are gone (Phase 3, step 2, the seventh family, the subject's own).** `reading.Subject(kind, players, teams, position)` on `Scope.subject` replaces `Scope.player`, `players`, `team`, `teams` and `Reading.position` (`reading.SubjectKind` the kinds; `Subject.player` and `Subject.team` the one player and the one team a reader reads; `Subject.from_slots`, `to_slots`, `slot_record`, `without_position`), and `subject.Subject` - the subject reading's record - IS one (the typed value as read, with the opponent, the own team, the companions, the evidence, the invented and filler names, the season named, the intent and why and the claims beside it). `subject.apply_subject` writes it, with the reading's kind and position group; the point reader takes the kind, the names and the position from it (`point.read_point` writes the reading's kind and position onto it for a Reading built by hand, and a position group narrows the league's own moves alone - `point._everyone_point`); the planner's `Query.position` is the point's subject's; every relation reader, entity settler and the coverage, calendar and fingerprint readers read `scope.subject`. The stages are handed `router.Named` (the typed subject, the opponent, the subject the question's grammar names - `subject.subject_named_in`, was `router._subject_named_in` - and the team nicknames the words hold - `subject.team_words_in`) and read no name from the words themselves; `router._MODEL_SLOTS` is gone (the freeze of scoping declarations 9 -> 8, its debt 4 -> 3) and `router.settle` refuses a name passed as a slot (its new `handed` keyword takes them); four stages that wrote a name the parser never hands - a rank word or a pseudo-team filed as the team (`_route_intent_slots`, `_route_team_slots`), a team in the players list (`_route_period_intents_player_beside_team`), one player listed as a comparison (in `_route_one_player_intents`) - are deleted, reaching none of the 2,710 readings. The family's words moved to the lexicon - `TEAM_NICKNAME`, `TEAM_CITIES`, `TEAM_ABBREVIATIONS` (were `router._TEAM_WORD`, `_TEAM_CITY`, `_TEAM_ABBREVIATION`), `SUBJECT_OF_HIGH`/`COUNT`/`HAVE`, `SUBJECT_WORDS`, `NOT_A_SUBJECT` (router), `TEAM_SINGULARS`, `POSITION_WORDS` and `POSITION_GROUPS` (were `subject.TEAM_SINGULARS`, `reading.POSITIONS`), `FILLER_PLAYER_WORDS` (reading), `NEVER_A_NAME`, `MEETING_WORDS`, `TWO_TEAMS_LOG_WORDS`, `TWO_TEAMS_RECORD_WORDS`, `AS_TYPED_WORD` (parse), `MAX_NAME_WORDS` (one cap where `subject._SPAN_MAX_WORDS` and `_MAX_NAME_WORDS` were two), `COMMON_WORDS_THAT_NAME_TEAMS`/`PLAYERS`, `MONTH_ABBREVIATIONS`, the child grammars' words (`CHILD_*`, `N_PLUS`), `NO_NAME_HAS`, `GAMES_NOT_SUMMARY`, `AGAINST_PHRASE`, `FOR_TEAM_PHRASE`, `VERSUS_WORD`, `LETTER_RUN`, `whole_phrases` - and `subject.py` compiles no pattern of its own (15 compiled and 25 lines reading `re` before; `is_team_name` and `team_named_in_text` moved there from the router). The subject reading claims the characters of the names it settled (`subject.subject_claims`: `player`, `team`, `opponent`, `tenure`, `position` claims on `Reading.claims` - 1,680 player, 354 team, 501 opponent, 14 tenure and 51 position claims on the 2,710 readings, two joined with a companion's as `opponent+player`). Measured first (`~/association-research/stages/subject_family.py`, the four slots at every place they are written on the 2,710 readings): the model's player spans and the words' names differ on 134 and the words win every one; the stages wrote a name after the subject reading on 58 (the grammar's subject 30, a team's nickname 27, a quarter's player 1) and no other stage fired; one player is never in the plural slot, two never in the singular, a list of teams never (so the count says which slot each projects to). No cell (no relation table declares a name); a behavioral test per relation. Proved on the four populations against `054d9e9`: 628 of 628 recorded questions, 2,082 of 2,082 feed answers and 2,710 of 2,710 readings identical through the projection with the one added record field, `reading.who`, ignored and listed by count; unit-test calls 2,634 of 2,648 identical aligned past the claims and the snapshot's `who`, the 14 others in 7 tests handing a router-era slot shape (a name listed alone in `players`, two teams split between `team` and `teams`) that the count projects as `player` or `teams`, every answer and refusal they assert unchanged; the subject harness re-run identical on 2,710 of 2,710; the normalizer's prompt and schema hashes unchanged; the ledger 702 of 2,409, identical line for line; the ratchets unchanged (`con_in_the_reader` 23). Tests: 2 deleted with the stages they tested (a team in the players list, a pseudo-team), 1 rewritten (a rank word beside a real team), 158 lines of 24 test files re-pointed at the typed subject (the stages' payload tests through `tests/routed.py`'s new `staged`, `staged_raw` and `handed`), 18 added (`test_subject_value.py`).

- **Breaking (Python API): the measure - what a question asks about - is one typed value read by one tagger from one catalog, and the seven slots that carried it are gone (Phase 3, step 2, the sixth filter family).** `reading.Measure(key, as_typed, how, unit, whose, side, shot_value, category, won, beside)` on `Scope.measure` replaces `stat`, `rate`, `per_game`, `side`, `shot_value`, `fields` and `kind`: `key` is one of the catalog's (`measure.CATALOG`, keyed by the closed `measure.MeasureKey`, 42 keys - the normalizer's spelling where it has one, the compiler's otherwise - each saying how the measure is read on each relation: the game column, the compiler's derived measure, the ranking's metric for a bare name, a career, a total and a per-game figure, the team metric, the opponent's team metric, its label), `as_typed` the spelling the reader wrote (the model's key, the grammar's, a stage's, a team metric's alias text - what a refusal prints and the `stat` slot projects to), `how` the rate asked (`per_game`, `total`, `per_100`, `per_90`), `unit` the rate's words (the `rate` slot's cell), `whose` own or opponent ("points allowed" is the opponent's points), `side` and `category` NetPoints only (a fingerprint metric named outright, `assist_o_net_pts`, is `netpoints` of the `assist` category on offense), `shot_value` the shots relation's (the measure's rather than the relation's cell: measured, a stat naming the same shots arrives beside it on 5 of 13 and the relation reads the value first), `won` a run's result (the `kind` slot: Jeff's open item 12, typed with the measure), `beside` the columns a ranking shows (`fields`). The six vocabularies are lookups into the catalog (`measure.ALIASES`, 390 spellings: the normalizer's 38 keys, the grammar's 29, `lexicon.MEASURE_WORDS`' 57, the team metrics' 130 alias texts, the leaderboard metrics' names, the compiler's derived names) through `measure.key_of`; `measures.resolve_metric`, `stat_measure`, `stat_column`, `log_extras`, `period_split_measure`, `streak_column` and `team_metrics.resolve_team_metric` take the `Measure` and read its facets (`measure.metric_name`, `measure_name`, `column_name`, `team_metric_name`), and `METRIC_ALIASES`, `CAREER_METRIC_ALIASES`, `MEASURE_ALIASES`, `WORD_MEASURES`, `measures._ALIASES` and `team_metrics.normalize_stat` are gone (`STAT_ALIASES` is `lexicon.STAT_ALIASES`, re-exported). `tests/query/measure_spellings.json` records what the four lookups returned for every one of 391 reachable spellings on `508d643`, and a test holds the catalog to it on the facets each vocabulary reached (a team alias text the team facet, a box-score abbreviation the game column, a key's own spelling all five); 12 spellings are unified on purpose and listed (`three_pt_pct`, `avg_points`, `plus_minus`, ... each a metric or derived name spelled outright, which no reader reached with the facets that moved). **One tagger:** `measure.read_measure(question, MeasureContext)` in `router._settle`, at the position of the last stage that wrote one of the seven (the side, after the lines), over the settled intent, the model's key as CONTEXT (`raw["stat"]`: the words' own measure stands over it - `measure.named`, the grammar `parse.measure` was, run before the intent stages too so the ones that turn on a games key read the same context - and where the words name none the key stands as it did, so no answer moves), the stat the lines tagger read beside a line and whether one is keyed, and a test's side, shot value and columns; it reproduces, in the stages' order, every writer the stages had - the intent-chosen keys (fouling out, a games count under a line's reader, a quarter's or a half's stat kept only where named), the model's key dropped on a whole-line reader where the words name no stat (`names_a_stat`, `router._named_a_stat` was), the advanced metrics, game score by the reader's spelling, a 2-point percentage, a ranking by shot distance (the `shot_distance` sentinel key), the attempts beside a make, the LONGEST team-metric alias the words hold (`team_metric_named`, `router._team_metric_in` was) with "allowed" after it, a NetPoints rate folded into its key and any other unit kept as the `rate` cell, a team's total, the stat beside a line, a run's result, a fingerprint's side, a chart's shots, the columns beside a ranking - and claims what it read (890 claims on the 2,710 readings; two stretches of one reading that overlap are one claim of it now, `span.claimed`, where 6 read as `measure+measure`). The cell (contract 4): `Measure.CELLS` is `rate` - a unit asked for, honored by the season-line ranking (a total, a NetPoints metric's per-100 form, any other unit refused by name as the `ranking_unit` cause) and the team compiler's unnarrowed total, declined by every other reader in the sentence it had ("the relation cannot honor ['rate']"); `STATED_SCOPING`'s ranking row and the planner's team-scalar cells name it through `Measure.CELLS`, `SCOPING_SLOTS` is `split` alone, and no relation table declares it (a unit narrows no games). `Scope.from_slots` still takes the seven (it builds the `Measure`, the spelling resolved through the catalog, a `side` or `shot_value` outside its set refused at the door), `to_slots` and `projected()` give the old shape back in the old field order (the seven where the fields stood, a side or a rate the key folds in left out, `kind` as `win`/`loss`), and the typed value is recorded beside the reading as `measure`. Measured first (`~/association-research/stages/measure_family.py`, the seven slots and the point's `measures`/`aggregate` as each stage set them on all 2,710 readings, the words that set them, which of the six vocabularies each resolves through, the planner's verdict and the relations' resolution): a stat on 1,004 readings in 69 spellings (the model's on 280, 23 distinct; the words' on 958, 37 distinct; the model and the words disagreeing on 58, the words winning every one; "model's key stands" on 32; the model's key dropped on 5, the words' on 22), a rate on 13, a per-game log on 38, a side on 1, a shot value on 13, columns beside a ranking on 7, a run's kind on 6; no stage moved a slot between the route and the reading; a key no answer-side vocabulary held on 24 (`shot_distance` 15, `games_played` 6, "rebounds allowed" 2, "assists allowed" 1 - refused by name, as before); the family's causes `needs_stat` 7, `shot_distance_ranking` 6, `unknown_stat` 6, `line_names_no_stat` 4, `ranking_unit` 2, `no_ranking_measure` 2, and the planner's `['rate']` decline on 4. Tests: `test_claimed_folds_a_nested_claim_and_joins_a_partial_overlap`, `test_a_word_two_readings_share_reads_both_and_raises_nothing` (`tests/query/test_span.py`).
- **One game named as his, in a phrasing the window grammar misses, is that game on every reader that honors an end.** "stephen curry shot chart for his last home game" drew the season's 23 home games (198 of 422 made) and "nikola jokic game log for his first road game" listed his LAST 10 road games, with nothing saying "last" or "first" went unread: the grammar's one-game rows allow only a season type between the word and "game", and the rule that reads "his last home game" as one game (`lexicon.SINGLE_GAME`: the end and a count of one) applied to a player's line alone. The window tagger applies it on the readers that honor an end too (`window._ONE_GAME_NAMED_INTENTS`: the log, the two charts, the two NetPoints readers - not the two period readers, where a quarter's ordinal sits exactly in the gap the rule allows: "his first quarter stats per game" would read as his first game), where the grammar read nothing: the chart draws the one game (2026-04-07 vs SAC) and the log lists the first road game. Measured first: 0 of the 2,710 readings name a game so on these readers, so no population answer moves (628 of 628, 2,082 of 2,082, 2,710 of 2,710 identical; 2,623 of 2,624 unit-test calls, the one move the window slice's); the two wordings above are the test (`tests/query/test_window.py`, `test_router.py`), answered on master `1599742` and on this tree. The claims ledger moves 694 -> 709 unread words (393 -> 402 questions), every one "regular" or "season" in "steph curry's last/most recent/final regular season game" (10 questions, the shot chart's and the NetPoints reader's): until now deleting either word turned the phrase into one the grammar's one-game row missed, so the whole window vanished and the word counted as read; the rule reads across them, and the span tagger's "regular season" is the type every reader defaults to, which the record cannot tell from unstated (`ROADMAP-TYPES.md`, "Still open" 8) - an overcount the ledger's own caveat names ("a word a rule matched and did not need"), exposed rather than a dependency lost. The rule says the count may not grow; this commit is its own so that call can be made on it alone.
- **The web page keeps its thread in the browser and rebuilds it at load (ISSUES.md #69).** Each answered turn - the question, the answer event as the server sent it, the trace lines - is kept in `localStorage` (the newest fifty), and the thread is rebuilt from it at load through the same code that renders a live answer, with the question-recall list rebuilt to match; a "forget history" control in the header clears it. Per browser, not shared (a server-side store would be the shareable version); storage missing or full leaves the live page unaffected. Since a reload now loses no answer, the live-reload rule relaxes to a draft or a question in flight, and the indicator's wording says the thread is kept. Four browser checks added and one reworded in `scripts/check_web_ui.py`; not a query-path change.

A sixteen-entry table spells those letters out first (`entities._FOLD_WHOLE_LETTERS`): "Asik", "Dordevic", "Soren". No recorded question or feed answer types one, so none moves; one test.

Now the parser reads them, once, in `parse.reading_from_route`, onto two new Reading fields: `Reading.refused` (`championship`; `no_player_reading`, facts `player` and `intent`) - planned by `plan_point` as the refusal ahead of the point's own and said before any reader runs, where it was - and `Reading.unsupported` (the draft's `Unsupported(what, as_typed)` filter, as causes: `playoff_round`, `non_calendar_situation` with `reads_as` `age`/`alignment`/`other`, `period_stat`, `period_as_condition`, `team_period_stat`, `bench_points`, `team_boolean_count`, each with the words as typed and the intent the page shows) - recognized whatever answers, the first said by `refusal_result` only where the answer side declined and the coverage floor did not refuse, so a question the compiler answers is answered. `reading.CAUSES` 18 -> 27; every sentence moved to `say.refusal_phrase` word for word (`say.CHAMPIONSHIP_REFUSAL`), and the page's values with it (`refused` and `intent`, or `named_player`, through `Refusal.shown`). The regexes went to the reader (`parse`), `measures.TEAM_PERIOD_COLUMNS` joined the reader's vocabulary (`team_games` re-exports it), and `entities.team_only_question_names_a_player` is the sayer's. Proved before deleting the old path: the old checks against the reader's causes said by the planner on every reading of the 2,710 (163 recognized, 7 refused) and on 3,834 hand-built readings across every check's branches - 0 differ, and a perturbed sentence fails 17. Moves, all of them: **628 recorded questions** - 7 readings: "show which team won the nba championship for the past 10 years" (`refused` championship; the planned query becomes the refusal); "most opponent bench points allowed in the west at home by team this month" (bench_points); "lebron ppg as an 18 year old" (non_calendar_situation, age); "2025 NBA Finals game schedule" and "nba finals game log 2025" (playoff_round); "oklahoma city thunder all-time triple doubles against the west" and "... vs west" (team_boolean_count) - each answer identical, text, data and remarks. **2,082 feed answers** - 163 readings, answers identical: refused championship 3 and no_player_reading 3 (each with its planned query), playoff_round 117, non_calendar_situation 32, bench_points 4, team_boolean_count 4 (the commit message lists every question). **2,710 readings** - 170, the same questions. **Unit-test calls** (aligned past the additions, `calls_aligned.py`): 2,556 compared, 2,546 identical, 10 moved - the Reading gaining `unsupported` or `refused` (and for the team-only player, the planned refusal) in the three agent tests of these shapes and one subject test's championship wording; 12 new `refusal_result` calls of the new kinds. Tests: `test_refusals.py` is `test_unsupported.py` (13 tests: 12 re-seated on the reader's causes and the planner's sentence with their cases unchanged, 1 a parser test already), 1 re-seated in `test_entities.py`, 1 renamed in `test_compose.py`, 0 deleted; the every-cause test holds the nine new kinds. Ratchets: `question_outside_the_reader` 10 -> 1 (`history.RunHistory.write`, the trace file's writer, which records the question and answers nothing), `regex_outside_the_reader` 6 -> 4, `con_in_the_reader` 23 -> 23.

- **`pip install association-py` works: 5.0.0 was the first version uploaded to PyPI (2026-10-09), through Trusted Publishing under the publisher registered for `association-py`.** The notes that said releases lived on GitHub only, and the install lines pinned to a release tag, are gone from `README.md`, `docs/installation.rst`, `docs/usage.rst` and `docs/releasing.rst`; the one-time `EXTRAS_PIN` rewrite in `scripts/bump_version.py` with them. `scripts/release.sh` passes the release notes through stdin at both points, since the 5.0.0 changelog section (293,016 bytes) was past the 128 KiB an argument or an environment variable may hold and the first attempt failed with "Argument list too long" before creating anything.

## 5.0.0 - 2026-10-09
- **Breaking (packaging): the distribution is `association-py` on PyPI; the import package, the `association` command and the repository keep the bare name.** PyPI refuses `association` as a project name though nobody holds it: no project row (its per-project RSS route answers 404, as for a made-up name), no release ever, no name confusable with it under PyPI's rule over its full index of 909,700 projects, and no standard-library module - of the four causes PyPI's help page lists, that leaves an administrator's prohibition. So `pip install association-py` (and `'association-py[web]'`) is the install command from this release on; `association.__version__` and `docs/conf.py` read the installed metadata under the new name; `association web --help` and the missing-extra hint say `pip install 'association-py[web]'`; the wheel is `association_py-X.Y.Z-py3-none-any.whl`. The releases before this one carry the old name in their metadata and stay on GitHub only. `scripts/bump_version.py` moves a tag-pinned `association[web] @ git+...` install line to the new name with its pin (`EXTRAS_PIN`), since pip and uv refuse a `name @ url` install whose metadata name differs; one test. Trusted Publishing is unchanged: the publisher on PyPI is registered for `association-py` (AGENTS.md, "Releasing").
- **Breaking (Python API): the answer side chooses a reader by the planned point's shape and a sayer by the body, never by an intent (the Phase 2 review's cleanup (b)6, "the Result is typed", third commit).** `compose.answer` picked a reader by `intent ==` (72 mentions of "intent" in `compose/__init__.py`), passed every reader `STATED_SCOPING[intent]` (23 sites), and `say()` was a decision list over the span's source, the relation, a facts key and the body. Now the planner settles what a point is read and said as - `compose.plan.PointShape(relation, shape, by)` (the target types' relation, shape and `by`; `player_periods` and `team_periods` name a quarter's read), by `plan.shape_of(intent, query)`, on the new `Planned.shape` - and `compose.answer` looks the reader up in one table by that key alone (`compose._ROUTES`; a route marked `only` is the point's only answer and declines rather than step aside). `STATED_SCOPING` is keyed by `PointShape`; `plan.SHAPE_WORDS` names each shape's retired words, and `plan.words_stated(name)` is the planner's lookup while it still reads intents. `say()` chooses from the headline body's type and the one field that says what it is (`Scalar.how`, `Grouped.by`, `Rows.by`, `Chart.kind`) through three tables; `Span.source` chooses nothing (a team's record tells a tally from a standings line by its detail part). The intent is read by the planner only where the query alone cannot tell two retired templates' words apart (a log from a quarter's, the league's ranking from a quarter's, a count's shapes, a team's own total tried on its season line first; `# Phase 3: needs the Reading's own shape and by`), and as `Planned.floor`, the coverage entry the point's season is checked against (`coverage.SOURCES` is still keyed by the retired words; `# Phase 3: needs the relation's declared tables`). "intent" in `compose/__init__.py`: 72 -> 6 mentions, all in prose; in `query/`: 671 -> 635 (the planner gained what the answer side lost). Identical on 628 of 628 recorded questions, 2,082 of 2,082 feed answers and 2,710 of 2,710 readings, text and remarks; 2,556 of 2,556 unit-test calls identical in every outcome, and 981 of them differ in one argument by construction - the `planned` value `compose.answer` is handed carries the two new fields (`shape`, `floor`), checked by stripping them: 0 differ. Tests: 0 deleted; the scoping tests read `words_stated(name)` and `SHAPE_WORDS` (9 files, by name), an empty log test gives its body; 1 added (the answer side names no intent - watched to fail).
- **Breaking (Python API): `Result.facts` is typed per shape, and the cells a read applied are typed values on the narrowing and the span (the Phase 2 review's cleanup (b)5, "the Result is typed", second commit).** `Result.facts` was a `Mapping[str, Any]` written at 51 constructions with about 80 distinct keys and read by the sayer at about 120 sites (inventoried at run time over the 628 recorded and 2,082 feed questions, `~/association-research/stages/facts_census.py`, and statically, `facts_inventory.py`). Each key is now one of three things. A cell the read applied is a typed value: the new `result.Cell` union (`Period`, `OnDate`, `Line`, `Role`, `GameOfSeries`, `Calendar`, `Companions`, `Met`, `ShotValue` - the minimal set the keys needed, declared by this step) on `Narrowing.cells`, read by type (`Narrowing.cell(kind)`, `lines()`, `period`), and `Span.since`/`until`/`ordinal`; a split's or a run's parameter is its body's (`Grouped.of`: the line a record splits by, the teammates a with/without split divides by; `Runs.line`/`won`: what a streak held along). A fact the sentence needs is a field of one frozen record per shape (`result.Facts`: `CountFacts`, `LogFacts`, `LineFacts`, `SplitsFacts`, `PeriodFacts`, `PeriodRankingFacts`, `TeamPeriodFacts`, `RankingFacts`, `RecordFacts`, `MatchupFacts`, `MeetingsFacts`, `TeamRecordFacts`, `TeamStatFacts`, `TeamRankingFacts`, `OutlookFacts`, `NetPointsFacts`, `ChartFacts`), read by the sayer through one accessor that raises on a record of the wrong shape. A key that only chose the sayer is gone: a period split's `"period" in facts` is its `Period` cell. Moved off the bag besides: the `about` page values of a player's line and splits (now read off the cells), a ranking's season and a fingerprint's (the span's), a period log's order and limit and a period's window (`Result.window`), a shot distance's one game (an `OnDate` cell and the window it ended), the outlook's and the NetPoints season's "nothing found" (an empty body of the shape, where a Result with no parts was). `Narrowing.period` is the `Period` cell (a label and its numbers, where it was a string); `player_games.Narrowed.lines` keeps each line as values beside its words. `Scalar.how` names every scalar's reduction (`season`, `per_shot`, `per_100`, `total`, `projection`, `ranked` beside `per_game`, `count`, `record`). Identical on all four populations, text and remarks: 628 of 628 recorded questions, 2,082 of 2,082 feed answers, 2,556 of 2,556 unit-test calls, 2,710 of 2,710 readings. Tests: 0 deleted; 10 hand-built Results in `test_say.py` and `test_templates.py` rewritten to the typed facts and cells; 1 added.
- **Breaking (Python API): a refusal found at RUN is typed - `result.Refusal(kind, facts)` and `result.Clarify` - and its sentence is the sayer's, one phrase per cause (the Phase 2 review's cleanup (b)1, "the Result is typed", first commit).** Until now a reader that found nothing to say returned a worded `Reply` (36 constructions in `compose/`, 6 in the relation modules), a `Result` with no parts and `facts["missing"]` (`compose/team_stats.py`, which `say` branched on), or a `Result.empty` sentence; now every reader returns `Result | Refusal | Clarify` and nothing outside `compose/say.py` writes a refusal's words. `Refusal.kind` is closed: a READ's causes are the new `result.RUN_CAUSES` (50 kinds: a season under a floor, no games in the span, none matching the narrowing, a teammate never seen, a team short of games for points allowed, why no fingerprint can be drawn, ...), a READING's stay `reading.CAUSES` (17) - two disjoint sets, held by a test, because a reading's cause is decided from the words before any table is read and is pinned by the readings population, while a read's is a fact found in the warehouse; one `Refusal` type carries either, and `say.refusal_phrase(kind, facts)` is the one table that words both (the planner's sentences moved there from `compose.plan`, whose `refusal_result` now says `refusal_of(cause)` through it). A Refusal also says what the page shows beside the sentence (`shown`) and under which keys (`under`), since the readers' pages differed and the answers' data is held identical. `Clarify(asked, candidates, kind, active, why)` is the question back - several on record by a name, or a name nothing matched with near spellings. Moved or reshaped on the public surface: `entities.clarification` and `entities.suggestion` are `compose.say.clarification`/`suggestion`; `entities.no_match` is `entities.unmatched`, returning a `Clarify` or a `name_unmatched` `Refusal`; `entities.clarify`/`resolved_player`/`resolved_team`/`optional_team` return a `Clarify` where they returned a worded `Reply`; `player_relation.no_narrowed_games` and `no_games`, `team_relation.condition_team_no_games` return a `Refusal`; `Result.empty` is a `Refusal`; `compose.core.Refused` carries the typed outcome; `fingerprint.FingerprintUnavailable` carries a cause and its facts (`kind`, `facts`) rather than a sentence; `coverage.floor_refusal`/`coverage_refusal` are `check_coverage` typed; `say.say_period_refusal`, `say_period_unread`, `say_team_period_*`, `say_period_rank_*`, `say_conference_refusal` and `rankings.leaderboard_shot_distance_refusal` are phrase-table entries. A combined record's half that was a refusal no longer has its words searched for wins and a "Note:" tail (none of the refusals a half can come back with carried either). Of the 614 answered recorded questions, the ones worded outside the sayer went 35 -> 7 (`~/association-research/stages/typed_census.py`); the 7 are `refusals.unanswerable`/`by_question`, which read the question's own text in the answering loop and move with Phase 3's first item.
