The reader raises `reading.PointRefused` with a `reading.Cause` now (`kind` from the closed `CAUSES`, plain `facts`: the stat, or the unit and count), `parse.with_point` puts the cause on the Reading, and `compose.plan.refusal_result` builds the same sentence and data from it when `plan_point` runs - `ROADMAP-TYPES.md`'s `Refusal(cause, facts)`, declared by the step that first needs it. `compose.move` no longer imports `TemplateResult` or `templates.players`; `no_ranking_for` lives in `compose.plan`, where `games_reading`'s answer-side refusal still calls it. Identical on 628 of 628 recorded questions (the ten refusals among them said word for word), every unit-test outcome (seven calls differ in the one field that holds a cause where a sentence was) and 2,710 readings old tree against new (the 628 corpus questions and 2,082 outside it: 2,067 StatMuse feed questions with no names, 15 franchise wordings) (14 refusals). Two tests of the reader's sentence assert the cause and the planner's sentence from it.
- **A cell a shape cannot honor is the planner's to decline, not the point reader's** (`ROADMAP.md`, Phase 1, the `read_point` move, step 3, first five sites; no answer moves). The point reader raised `Unsupported` while reading when the point's own answerer could not honor a cell: a comparison over the season line with any narrowing, the with/without split with one its words do not state, and a quarter's split, a run or two players' meetings with a cell their retired template excluded. Those five checks are `compose.plan._shape_declines` now, run by `plan` before the relation's own cell check with the same sentence; the reader writes the point regardless, and the adapters stamp the point with the intent it is the default of. 26 of 2,710 readings old tree against new (the 628 corpus questions and 2,082 outside it: 2,067 StatMuse feed questions with no names, 15 franchise wordings) and 3 of 628 recorded ones carry a point where they declined before, each declined by the planner with the reason it was declined with; every query, result and answer identical. Three tests of the adapters' refusals assert on the planner's.
- **The measures are closed by name in `query/measures.py`** (`ROADMAP.md`, Phase 1, the `read_point` move, step 2; no answer moves). The point reader learned a measure's name by importing the SQL that computes it: `compose.core.COLUMNS` and `DERIVED`, `compose.team.GAME_MEASURES` and `SEASON_MEASURES`, `templates.common.HISTORY_COLUMNS`, and it compared `DERIVED`'s SQL text to a line to know that "fouled out" is six fouls. The names live in `measures` now - `GAME_COLUMNS`, `DERIVED_MEASURES`, `DERIVED_LINES` (`fouled_out` is `("fouls", 6)`), `BOOLEAN_MEASURES`, `LINE`, `TEAM_GAME_MEASURES`, `TEAM_SEASON_MEASURES`, `HISTORY_STATS` - the SQL tables stay where they run, keyed by exactly those names, and `tests/query/test_measures.py` holds the two sides together (it fails when `DERIVED_LINES` says five fouls). `compose.core` re-exports `COLUMNS`, `LINE` and `BOOLEAN_MEASURES`. This is the closed Measure type `ROADMAP-TYPES.md` asks for, as far as names go. Identical on 628 of 628 recorded questions, every unit-test outcome and 2,710 readings old tree against new (the 628 corpus questions and 2,082 outside it: 2,067 StatMuse feed questions with no names, 15 franchise wordings).
- **Five of the reader's seven imports of the answer side are gone; the two left are the point reader** (`ROADMAP.md`, Phase 1, step 6's last item, first half; no answer moves). What the reader took from the answer side was vocabulary and intent sets that lived there by accident of history, and each now lives on the reader's side under the same name, with the old module re-exporting it: `entities.team_named_in` (the team word's reader, from `compose.team`); `reading.PLAYER_REQUIRED_INTENTS`, `SUBJECT_RESTORABLE_INTENTS`, `OWN_TEAM_RESTORABLE_INTENTS`, `POSITIONS` and `FILLER_PLAYER_WORDS` (from `templates.common`); `measures.STAT_ALIASES` with its alias table (from `team_metrics`, whose catalog still keys on the same names) and `measures.PERIOD_COLUMNS` (from `player_games`). `[tool.importlinter]`'s list of the reader's imports is two: `parse -> compose.core` and `parse -> compose.move`, for `read_point`. The ratchets: `compose.team` no longer imports `re` (the regex ratchet shrank to 8), and the listed `compose.team:team_named_in` is `entities:team_named_in` - the same function under its new module, swapped in the list by hand rather than counted as new; its letter-run regex is `entities._LETTER_RUN`, since `_TEAM_WORD` and `_NAME_WORD` are names `router` already defines for other patterns (the one-concept gate caught both). Proved identical on 628 of 628 recorded questions, every unit-test outcome and 2,710 readings old tree against new (the 628 corpus questions and 2,082 outside it: 2,067 StatMuse feed questions with no names, 15 franchise wordings).
- **The reader always writes the condition it read; the answer refuses one it cannot honor** (`ROADMAP.md`, Phase 1, step 6's second item; no recorded answer moves). A teammate's role - a start, the bench, a line reached, a player on the other side - was written into the Reading only where the answering template honored `conditions` (`subject._apply_conditions_honored`, read from `HONORED_SCOPING` and `compose.COMPILED_INTENTS`), and the parser gated its own two readers of those phrases on the same question; on any other intent the role was read and then dropped, and the misread split it left behind was what refused the question, where anything did. "how many times did the 76ers beat boston when embiid started" answered every meeting (2-2), the start gone without a word, and "plot jokic's fingerprint in games murray started" drew the season. The condition is written whatever the intent now, and `check_scope` or the planner refuses it by name ("head_to_head cannot honor ['conditions']"). The subject reader's import of `compose` is gone with the check: the reader's imports of the answer side are seven. Proved on 628 of 628 recorded questions and every unit-test outcome (identical), and on 2,710 wordings old tree against new (identical readings; none of them names a role on an intent that dropped it, which is why the two wrong answers above were found by hand).
- **The stages run once per question** (`ROADMAP.md`, Phase 1, step 6's first item; no answer moves). The parser ran the router's stages under the parent intent its grammar named, then again under each child the subject's shape and the question's words named to see whether the stages kept it, and once more under the one that did; the subject reading ran them too, under "other", before the parser ran them at all - 1.68 runs a question on average, up to four. Now `subject.child_named` names the child from the grammar alone, `parse._read_route_staged` runs the stages ONCE under it, and only where they decline it (a history with no stat named is the whole line: 4 of the 628 recorded questions) runs them under the parent. `subject.read_subject` reads and decides nothing (its ``intent`` is the caller's); `subject.settle_subject(subject, intent, *, parent, words)` writes the intent and why with no stage run; the Route carries the settled subject and `parse.reading_from_route` settles nothing. The Reading's decisions say the child the words named (and a child the stages declined); they no longer list the slots a second run moved, since there is none. Proved on the 628 recorded questions (scope, point, query, result and answer identical; 172 readings differ only in decisions and in `subject.intent_reason`, which the Reading now carries), on every unit-test outcome (the same fields, and the six tests of a helper that bypassed the parent's stages until now), and on 2,710 wordings old tree against new, among them the StatMuse feed with no names: three read a stat the old child run had missed ("kyrie career 5 3s games on road" answers where it was refused). The claims ledger reads 690 unread words where it read 683: seven were counted as read only because a decision record named the slots a second run had moved.
- **The SQL ratchet counts statements, and the D4 freeze holds every shape the decision names** (`ROADMAP.md`, Phase 1's order from here, step 4; no code under `src/` changes). `scripts/check_ratchets.py` counted a module that executes SQL as one violation, so a listed module could add statements without the gate noticing; it counts the `.execute` and `.sql` calls per module now (103 in 19 modules, `scripts/ratchets.json`), fails on a count that grew as on a new module, and `--shrink` lowers a count as it removes a name. `tests/query/test_frozen_shapes.py` froze the 25 intents alone where decision D4 says "no new intent, template, presenter, scoping table or per-intent renderer": it now holds the 12 templates, the 12 presenters and the team-only one, the 10 adapters, the 12 scoping declarations (every module-level name under `query/` matching SCOPING, STATED or `_SLOTS`, read from the source) and the page's 22 renderers, each watched to fail when one is added.
- **The stage snapshot's `query` stage is what the planner built, and its first line says which Python, DuckDB and ollama ran** (`ROADMAP.md`, Phase 1's order from here, step 3; no answer moves). The `query` record was the Reading's point projected again, so a planner that built something else from the point - which is what PLAN will do once it resolves names - would have gone unseen; it is now the planned `Query` or `TeamQuery` as plain values (`relation`, `skeleton`, `measures`, `scope`, ...), and the point the reader read moves into the `reading` record as `point`. A test hands the snapshot a planning whose query differs from its point and sees the difference in the `query` stage. `scripts/stage_snapshots.py run` writes `python`, `duckdb` and `ollama` (version, model, digest) into the meta line, and `compare` warns when two runs differ in any of them - the recorded replies were said by one ollama build on one machine, and a lowering or a sort can move with the interpreter or the engine. Proved stage by stage against the tree before: `reading` (without the point), `result`, `answer` and `remarks` identical on 628 of 628, and the old `query` record equal to the new `reading.point` on every one of the 452 questions that have a point. The stored baselines are re-recorded in the new shape.
- **Breaking: the compiler takes its planning, and a name is looked up inside a block or not at all** (`ROADMAP.md`, Phase 1's order from here, step 2; no answer moves). Two paths a step had kept beside the one it built, each taken only by tests and scripts. `compose.answer(ctx, reading, *, planned, ...)` requires the PLAN stage's verdict (`compose.plan.plan_point`), where it planned the Reading itself when `planned` was left out; `stages.read_stages` requires it too, and `stages.snapshot` raises `ValueError` for a Reading handed over without one (`scripts/claims_ledger.py` plans what it reads). `names.loaded()` takes no connection and serves each connection used inside it; a lookup outside a block raises `names.NotLoaded`, where it read its table again for every lookup - the same answers at a statement apiece, and nothing to say a caller had forgotten the block. `Agent.ask` enters one per question, as before; every test runs inside one (`tests/conftest.py`), and 901 of them looked a name up outside one until then. Tests plan through `tests/routed.py`'s `planned_answer` (five files' copies of one helper). Proved on both populations: 628 of 628 recorded questions and every one of 1,389 unit-test outcomes identical; the planner still runs once and the reader still issues two statements a question (the two loads); the ledger still reads 683 of 2,409. The unit-test recorder masks a test's own temporary directory now: pytest numbers two tests with one long name prefix in the order its workers reach them, which moved one recorded path between runs of one tree.
- **Breaking: `Agent.ask` takes no `route`, and a route with no subject is not read for again** (`ROADMAP.md`, Phase 1's order from here, step 1; ISSUES.md #288 closed; no answer moves). `Agent.ask(question, route=...)` answered a recorded route in place of reading the question, and `parse.reading_from_route` read a subject of its own for such a route - the old third reading, kept beside the one `read_route` makes, on a different scope (the settled one), which is how the two paths came to disagree about a franchise's old name. Both are gone, with `Route.from_slots` (the replay's door) and `parse._read_route_folded_scope` (the apostrophe fold a replayed route's slots needed; `read_route` folds its own). `reading_from_route` raises `ValueError` for a route that carries no subject. `scripts/preview_answers.py` answers recorded questions through the whole agent with the normalizer's recorded reply in the model's place (`--from-live` and `--from-history` read the `(normalizer)` trace line; `--case QUESTION NAMES_JSON STAT`), as `scripts/stage_snapshots.py` does. Tests hand the agent a route at the reader's boundary instead (`tests/routed.py`: `ask_routed` stands in for `read_route`; `with_subject` reads the subject the way `read_route` does): 39 call sites moved there, 2 tests whose subject was the door itself deleted (a recorded route answered unread; a replayed route's apostrophes), and the replay halves of 2 more. Proved on both populations: 628 of 628 recorded questions identical, and of 1,388 unit-test calls every outcome identical but five whose one-letter question ("q") a too-short refusal now stops, lengthened.
- **A team is read in the season the question names** (ISSUES.md #316, the player's own team and the opponent; a regression of this cycle's "the subject is read once"). The parser reads who the question is about before the stages settle the season, so the scope it read from held none, and a franchise's old name was read as of today: "chris paul assists for the hornets in 2008" asked "'Charlotte Hornets' matches more than one team - did you mean New Orleans Hornets or Charlotte Bobcats?", where it had answered 11.6 assists a game with the New Orleans Hornets until the three subject readings became one. `subject.read_subject` now reads the question's own season (`season_text.season_from_text`) where the scope holds none. The opponent's half was never right and is fixed with it: "kobe points against the hornets in 2008", "lakers record against the hornets in 2011" and "lebron stats vs the bobcats in 2012" answer where both trees asked. Neither proof population holds such a wording - 628 of 628 recorded questions and 1,386 of 1,386 unit-test calls are identical before and after - so it is held by `test_a_team_is_read_in_the_season_the_question_names`, on ESPN's own franchise ids, watched to fail. Still open under #316: a team that is the SUBJECT under an old name ("what was the bobcats record against the hornets in 2012").
- **Breaking: Python 3.14 or newer is required, and the interpreter is pinned.** `requires-python` said `>=3.10` and nothing tested it: CI ran on its runner's own 3.12.3, and a devbox with no pin took whatever `uv` found newest. `.python-version` now pins 3.14 (`uv sync` reads it locally and in CI), `requires-python` is `>=3.14`, and ruff, mypy and pyright target it - which rewrote five `except (A, B):` clauses without their parentheses, `timezone.utc` as `datetime.UTC`, and three generic functions with type parameters (`cli.commands._query_engine_options`, `templates.common._apply_situation`, `whole_span`). `uv.lock` loses the older interpreters' markers and `exceptiongroup`. Found on the first run on the new devbox (Jeff's call, 2026-10-02).
- **`names.sql_lower` is DuckDB's `lower()` on any interpreter** (ISSUES.md, found the same day; no answer moves). It lowered with `str.lower()`, one code point at a time, which agrees with DuckDB only while Python's Unicode tables are the version DuckDB bundles: against DuckDB 1.5.5, Python 3.12 and 3.13 agreed on every code point, 3.10 (Unicode 13) and 3.14 (Unicode 16: U+1C89, U+A7CB, the Garay capitals - 27 code points) did not, and `test_lowering_is_duckdbs_over_every_code_point` was red on both. The mapping is now DuckDB's own, asked of it once by `scripts/gen_duckdb_lower.py` and committed as `query/duckdb_lower.py` (`LOWER_RUNS`: 1,433 code points in 182 runs); the same test compares it with the installed DuckDB over every code point, so a DuckDB upgrade that moves it fails the suite rather than drifting. No name on record holds a letter the two disagreed on.
- **The reader's last three name statements come from the index: two statements per question, both loads** (`ROADMAP.md`, Phase 1, contract 3; no answer moves). After the entity module's lookups moved to `query.names`, three statements were still issued per word: the team compiler's `team_named_in`, the subject reading's `_team_abbreviation` and the parser's `_classify_span_abbreviation`. `entities.teams_named_by_word` and `entities.team_abbreviations` answer them from the teams' index. Over the 277 yardstick questions the reader issued 10,658 statements before the index (38.5 a question), 2,689 with it, and 554 now - the two loads, once per question. Checked against the code before it over every question, every word of the 628 questions and every team's names: 1,600 and 942 inputs, no difference. `parse` and `subject` no longer execute SQL (the ratchet's list goes from 21 modules to 19), and `scripts/claims_ledger.py` reads inside `names.loaded` as `Agent.ask` does.
- **Who stands beside the subject has one reader, and a with/without split names every teammate the question does** (`ROADMAP.md`, Phase 1; ISSUES.md #310 closed). The stages read the names after "with", "without" and "when ... play" with regexes of their own, beside the subject reading's companions, and the two disagreed: "When Embiid plays with Paul George, what is the PHI record?" answered with and without Embiid alone, "this year, what is the Hornets' record when Brandon Miller, Lamelo, and Knueppel play?" for two of the three, and "PHI's record when Embiid and Paul George are both in the game" was refused ("with_without needs exactly one teammate, got []"). The stages' readers are gone (`router._played_together`, `_played_together_absent`, `_names_after`): `router.settle` takes who the subject reading found beside the subject (`router.Beside`, from `subject.beside`) and writes `without` and `with_player` from it. The subject's own reading gained what the stages' had: every name of a phrase by its position (`subject._name_segments`: "Tatum, Brown and Holiday" is three, an ordinary word two players share included), a name nobody resolves kept as typed for an absence so it is refused by name, a misspelled companion read where it is one player's near spelling ("without wembyanama"), and "with and without X" read from its "without". Measured against `c50c35a`: of 628 recorded questions 4 answers move, each to exactly the answer its graded sibling wording gives; 14 differ only in a companion written as the known player ("Joel Embiid") where the stage wrote the typed word; 610 are identical. Of 1,386 unit-test calls across a stage boundary 26 differ, all in those names. Over 25 wordings outside the corpus, each read with the model's names and with none, the count of names and the intent are what they were. Tests: 11 cases of the stages' name reading deleted with it, their wordings moved to the subject's tests (13 cases); 9 stage and parser tests now hand the stages the companions.
- **Names are recognized from an in-memory index, not by a statement per word** (`ROADMAP.md`, Phase 1, contract 3; no answer moves). Every lookup in `query/entities.py` that read only `players` or `teams` - the whole-word span matches behind `players_named_in`, the near-spelling pass, `find_players`, `find_teams`, the team-name, nickname and run-together readings, the grounding check - is answered from the new `query/names.py`: `PlayerIndex` and `TeamIndex`, each built from one statement (`SELECT athlete_id, display_name FROM players`, `SELECT * FROM teams`) and holding the rows in table order, each name's words split as `regexp_split_to_array` split them, a word -> rows map, and a vocabulary that `rapidfuzz.process.extract` searches once per word for near spellings. It reproduces DuckDB where Python differs: `lower()`'s simple per-code-point mapping, `damerau_levenshtein` over UTF-8 bytes ("č" is two edits from "c"), RE2's case folding (the Kelvin sign is a "k"), `ILIKE` with no escape character and, on a column whose statistics say it holds only ASCII, ASCII-only lowering ("İndiana" matches no team), and the `CatalogException`/`BinderException` a warehouse without `teams` or without its `name` and `location` columns raised. `Agent.ask` enters `names.loaded(con)` once per question, inside which each table is read at most once; outside it every lookup reads its table again, and an index already built from the same rows is reused. One order is defined where it was not: two players of one name (21 names on record, "Chris Smith", "Dee Brown") come in table order, where `ORDER BY display_name` left them to DuckDB's sort, whose order for them changed with which rows were sorted. Proved against `c50c35a`: 478,304 calls of 31 lookups over the corpus's words and spans, every player's names, 10,890 one-letter drops, doubles and swaps of 600 surnames and every team name differ in nothing but that tie (30, all in `find_players(..., limit=None)`); 628 of 628 recorded questions and 1,386 of 1,386 unit-test calls across a stage boundary are identical. The reader's statements over the 277 yardstick questions fall from 10,658 (38.5 a question) to 2,689 (9.7); 1,866 of those left are `compose.team.team_named_in`'s one statement per word, which reads `teams` itself.
- **The subject is read once per question** (`ROADMAP.md`, Phase 1; no answer moves). The parser read who the question is about three times - before the intent was known, again to choose a child intent, and again in its last step - each asking the warehouse for the same names, and on 18 of the 628 recorded questions the three disagreed. Now `parse.read_route` reads it once and the route carries it (`Route.subject`); `subject.settle_subject(subject, intent, question, scope)` decides what depends on the intent the stages settled (two teams meeting under `head_to_head`, the child a subject's shape and words name) and folds in a companion only the stages named (a misspelled "without wembyanama"), reading no name and asking the warehouse nothing. `parse.reading_from_route` settles the carried subject and reads one only for a replayed route. Proved on both populations against `7f16b2d`: of 628 recorded questions every planned query, result and answer is identical, 5 differ in the subject record (a companion named as typed where the third reading had seen the resolved name, a model's filler name recorded, a bogus player gone) and 185 in a decision's reason text, which now says what the one reading rested on; of 1,383 unit-test calls across a stage boundary none returns a different scope, intent, result or answer.
- **Every remark the templates write carries its kind and facts** (`ROADMAP.md`, Phase 0 closed; no answer moves). The 98 places a caveat, a stated default or a definition is written - in `templates/players`, `games`, `splits`, `teams`, `shots`, `netpoints`, `shotchart`, `fingerprint`, and the shared writers before them - pass their sentence through `notes.note` or `notes.decided`; 28 kinds, each with a closed set of fact names (`notes.FACTS`), checked whoever is listening and over every call in the source. Over the 628 recorded questions 180 answers now carry 234 typed remarks of 17 kinds (the rest of the kinds are reached only by the unit tests), every stage of every answer is identical to before, and two answers are found to drop a remark they wrote (a record over both season types loses each half's floor; filed).
- **The planner runs once per question, after the parser, not inside it** (`ROADMAP.md`, Phase 1, first step; no answer moves). `parse.with_point` planned the point it read to learn whether the relation could honor it, and `compose.answer` planned it again to answer. Now the parser only reads the point; `compose.plan.plan_point(reading)` is the PLAN stage - the query on its relation, or why there is none (`Planned.declined`, `Planned.refusal`) - run once by `Agent.ask` (`Agent.planned`) and handed to `compose.answer(..., planned=)`, which plans only for a caller that brings a Reading alone. A Reading whose narrowing the relation cannot honor now holds its point, and the planner's reason is on the planning, not on `Reading.point_declined`. `parse` no longer imports `compose.plan`: the reader's listed imports of the answer side go from nine to eight. Proved on both populations against `0155df8`: 628 of 628 recorded questions identical in every stage, text and remarks included; of 1,378 unit-test calls across a stage boundary, 8 differ, each the Reading or the keyword just described, and no returned answer.
- **What an answer says beside its numbers is recorded as a kind and its facts, where it is written** (`ROADMAP.md`, Phase 0's last item; no answer moves). `query.notes` holds the closed kinds: a `Note` is about the data or a term the answer uses (`games_unseen`, `floor`, `lines_rebuilt`, `definition` ...), and a decision the answer states is a `decisions.Decision` with a `kind` (`name_reading`, `season_redirected`, `minimum` ...), what else it could have been (`instead_of`) and its `facts` - Jeff's split, 2026-10-01: "could the question have said it differently?". A writer wraps the sentence it was already writing (`notes.note(kind, text, **facts)`, `notes.decided(...)`), gets it back unchanged, and inside `Agent.ask`'s collector the kind and facts are kept: on `Answer.notes` and `Answer.decisions`, on the wire (`AnswerResponse.notes`; a decision gains `kind`, `instead_of`, `facts`), and in the stage snapshot's `remarks`, which `scripts/stage_snapshots.py compare` holds identical whenever both runs recorded them. `Agent.unsaid` and `stage_snapshots.py remarks` name a remark that was written and never reached its answer. A fact is a plain value (a number, a string, a list of them) and a kind is a literal from the closed sets, both checked whoever is listening and, for the kind, over every call in the source.
- **Which words of a question the reading depends on, measured** (`ROADMAP.md`, Phase 0, contract 2; no answer moves). `scripts/claims_ledger.py` reads each of the 628 recorded questions whole and again with each content word deleted, and reports the words whose deletion leaves the reading and the planned query unchanged - from outside the reader, so the count means the same after the reader is replaced. `query.stages.read_stages(reading)` is the two records it compares. Baseline at `011091f`: 679 of 2,415 content words (28.1%) in 390 questions; eleven questions have an unread number, three of them fluent answers to a broader question (filed in `ISSUES.md`). `ROADMAP-TYPES.md` is the target types drafted for review (the Reading's typed filters, the Measure, the Query, the Result, five shapes and the note kinds, from an inventory of the 69 remarks the code writes today).
- **The directions the new roadmap set are gates** (`ROADMAP.md`, Phase 0; no answer moves). Three import contracts hold the query package to its stages while the packages they will live in do not exist: the reader (`normalizer`, `parse`, `router`, `subject`, `season_text`) does not import the answer side, with today's nine violations listed by name; `compose.sentence` imports no `duckdb`; the answer side never reaches the normalizer. `scripts/check_ratchets.py` (the eighteenth gate) holds what an import cannot say, each as a list of today's violations in `scripts/ratchets.json` - 50 functions outside the reader that take the question, 21 modules that execute SQL, 91 private names the compiler imports from `templates/`, 9 modules outside the reader that import `re` - and fails on a new one and on a listed one that is gone, so each list only shrinks. `tests/query/test_frozen_shapes.py` holds decision D4: the 25 intents the reader can name are frozen.
- **The trace says what will answer, and five docstrings describe the tree that exists** (ISSUES.md #284). The route's trace line ended " - not ported yet" for every intent outside `TEMPLATES` - 206 of 277 yardstick answers, all of them the compiler's; it now ends "- a template", "- the compiler" or "- no reader: refused unless a named refusal has its cause". The module docstrings of `templates`, `compose`, `compose.core` and `compose.present` said seven intents were compiled (thirteen), that streaks were out of scope (the `run` shape), that the pipeline tried a template first, and that the presenters read nothing of their own (most call a template body's SQL); each now says what the code does, with the measured split. `router._AGENT_ONLY`, named for the agent deleted in 5.0.0, is `_QUARTER_WORDS`.
- **Each stage's output per question, as a record that can be compared** (`ROADMAP.md`, Phase 0; no answer moves). `query.stages.snapshot(reading, answer)` is one question's four records as plain values - the reading the parser settled, the point the compiler plans, the result's values, the answer - and `stages.differences(before, after)` every place two such records disagree, in stage order, so the first one names the stage a change entered at (floats within `FLOAT_TOLERANCE`, an int against a float a difference, the same rows in another order named as `reordered`, the sentences left out with `wording=False`). `Agent.reading` is the Reading the last question settled into, kept beside `Agent.unanswered` so the record needs no trace line parsed. `scripts/stage_snapshots.py run` answers the 628 recorded questions through the whole agent with the normalizer's recorded replies (no model), the date pinned, DuckDB single-threaded and chart paths masked; `compare` reports the first stage each question differs in and exits 1 on any difference, 2 when nothing was compared. The second population, every call the unit tests make across a stage boundary, is recorded by running the suite with `ASSOCIATION_STAGE_CALLS=<dir>` (`tests/stage_calls.py`) and compared with `compare-calls`. Measured on `7f6425b`: two runs of each population compare identical (628 of 628 questions, text included; 1,363 of 1,363 calls), and one perturbed token in a copy of the code fails each comparison at the stage it was made in.
- **A question that names no season reads the latest season with games on record, not the calendar's.** From 2026-10-01 `current_season()` returned 2027 - the calendar turns over on October 1, weeks before the first game and longer before a warehouse is loaded - so "how many points does luka average" answered "no 2027 regular season numbers", a comparison printed a table of dashes headed 2027, and the bare-name recency rule had nobody who "played this season" to prefer (79 of 84 sampled yardstick questions naming no season moved, measured with the date faked). `Agent.ask` now reads `query.connection.latest_season_on_record` (the latest season with a played regular-season or postseason game; preseason and unplayed games do not count) and answers inside `nba.season.season_on_record`, which caps `current_season()` at it; the trace says "default season: 2026 (the calendar's 2027 has no games on record)". The answer names the season it read, as before, and a season named in the question reaches any other. Outside the answering loop nothing is capped: the fetch path pulls `calendar_season()`. `nba.season.today` reads `ASSOCIATION_TODAY` (an ISO date) before the machine's date, so a harness can pin the day and a test can ask about one that has not come.
- **A team's point is held to the team relation's own cells.** "raptors game log in games where they made 5 threes in the first quarter" listed the Raptors' last ten games with the condition nowhere in the answer, and "raptors last 10 games ... as a starter" the same: `compose.plan` checked a team point against the PLAYER relation's scoping set, so a cell only a player's games carry (a period condition, a starter half, a teammate's role, a line on a box-score column, an ordinal season) passed the planner and was ignored by a relation with no such cell, and a team SUM was not checked at all. `compose.core._check_relation_scoping` reads `TEAM_RELATION_SCOPING` for a team subject, for every team shape, plus what that shape's own reader takes (`compose.plan._team_shape_cells`); it is an allow list, so a cell added to one relation is refused on the other until it is built there. The refusal says "a team's games cannot be narrowed by [...]".
- **Players beside the subject are conditions, on either side, any number of them** (ROADMAP step 3; Jeff's call, 2026-09-30, re-scoping "the pair as a compiler subject" and "the opponent-side condition"). The relation already had the one mechanism - a `Condition` on the games, a player with a side and a predicate, ANDed - and the pair's second player was a special case of it. Now a player after "vs"/"against"/"versus" is an opponent-side `played` condition wherever the words ask for the subject's games rather than the pair's summary (`subject._versus_companions`: a high, a count, a record, a log, a streak, splits, "most"/"fewest"; or three names or more): "most points by curry vs lebron" lists his best meetings (`compose.move._move_single_game`, "fewest" ascending), "how many times did lebron score 30 vs kawhi" counts them (7, over his career), "jay huff game log vs Embiid" is his games against Embiid, "giannis points per game vs lebron and curry" the games both played against him. The route carries them typed (`parse._read_route_versus`), so the reading's second pass keeps a name two players share. "curry vs lebron" and "curry stats vs lebron" stay the matchup summary. "Without X" is settled where the name is resolved (`templates.common._absence_condition`): X's missed games on the subject's team, or - where X was never his teammate in the span and the games are narrowed to an opponent X played for - X's missed games on the other side, bounded to his time on that team and said as "without X on the other side" ("steph curry game log vs lakers without lebron"); a versus team keeps such a question off the with/without split (`parse.PARENT_GRAMMAR`). An empty splits read narrowed by anything names the narrowing ("played 43 games, none of them vs LeBron James") instead of "listed in 43 box scores but did not play in any of them", a refusal that named the wrong missing fact; and "per game vs" no longer reads as a game log.
- **`period_leaderboard` ranks against an opponent or at a venue** (ROADMAP step 2, #185). "Who led the league in 1st quarter scoring against the Celtics this season" was refused: the relation already narrowed the pool, but the twenty-game qualifier disqualified everyone against one opponent. Jeff's call (2026-09-30): a narrowed pool keeps a SHARE of the games the narrowing leaves - half of the most anyone played in it, capped at the season's own minimum and never under one (`templates.games._period_leaderboard_minimum`) - and the answer names both ("minimum 2 games, half of the 4 anyone played") beside the narrowing ("in the 2026 regular season vs the Boston Celtics at home"). The four-quarter league table reads the same share off its pool. A range of seasons and a single date stay refused, by their reasons.
- **A quarter or half as a condition on which games count** (ROADMAP step 2, #275). "vj edgecombe three points made per game after making one three in first quarter" (yardstick-v2 F062) asks his whole-game threes over the games whose first quarter held one; it was refused by name, and before the guard a period read answered his first-quarter threes. `Scope.period_condition` (a `PeriodCondition`: the stat, the threshold, the comparison and a period or half) is read from the words by `parse.read_period_condition` - "after making one three in first quarter", "in games where he scored 10+ points in the first half", "when he makes a three in the 4th" - and its words are taken out of the question the grammar and the stages see, so the rest reads as the average, log or count it is. A bare number is exactly that many (the key's reading: "one three" is one, not one or more) and "at least N", "N+", "N or more" and "a" are at-least lines; the answer says which ("in games with exactly 1 3-pointer in the 1st quarter"), so the other reading is one word away. The relation applies it once for every reader (`Narrowed.narrow_period_condition`: one more clause, an EXISTS over the period's own rebuilt line summed over the games the base clauses select, so a log, an average, a count, a ranking and the box-score notes all honor and say it), for a named player and the league alike; a column rebuilt from the plays is refused where the warehouse holds none rather than read as zero. `period_split`'s presenter steps aside for one (its words say the one quarter measured), so "first quarter points in games he made a fourth-quarter three" is the compiler's own sentence, which names both; a matchup refuses it (a meeting is both players' whole game). The refusal (`refusals._period_as_condition`) now fires only where the words say a condition and no line could be read, and says what a readable one looks like. Measured on the warehouse: 28 games at 2.4 with exactly one first-quarter three, 36 at 2.8 with one or more; the key says 31 at 2.52.
- **A named player's four quarters side by side** (ROADMAP step 2, #162). "Jokic points by quarter" and "points per quarter for Luka" reached `other` and were refused (the router's `_BY_QUARTER` words were read only with no player named). Now `period_split` with no period is the breakdown: `Reading.group` gains `"period"`, the player relation's own group, and `compose.core._compile_by_period` compiles it as one statement - the union of four reads of the SAME narrowed games (the opponent, the venue, the window, every clause applied once), each seeing one quarter's line through the relation's own period narrowing, so a quarter he did nothing in is a zero over a game he played and the count is the same in every column. Said in the period templates' words (`templates.games._period_split_by_quarter_from`, the one-player counterpart of `_period_leaderboard_by_quarter`): per game and total in each quarter and in regulation, or a rate's percentage and made-attempted, "Overtime is no quarter and is not counted", and the season's measured accuracy. The stage (`router._route_period_intents_choose`) assigns the intent where a player and the "by/per/each/every quarter" words are read (`_AGENT_ONLY` gains "each"/"every quarter"); "Jokic qtrs" names neither a period nor the breakdown and is still refused. `player_games.REGULATION_QUARTERS` is the one definition of the four, shared with the league's table.
- **A shooting percentage in a quarter or half is answered, for a player and for a team** (ROADMAP step 2, the period relation's leftovers). "vj edgecombe 1st quarter 3pt percentage by game" (yardstick-v2) was refused as a stat the period's line does not rebuild; the line holds the makes and the attempts, so the percentage is the ratio of the two sums over the games - never a mean of per-game rates - `templates.games.PERIOD_RATES`, keyed by the compiler's own measure names (`fg_pct`, `three_pct`, `ft_pct`), which `_check_period_measures` already allowed. `_period_split_measure` and `_team_quarter_points_measure` read the normalizer's `fieldGoalPct`/`threePointFieldGoalPct`/`freeThrowPct` (`PERIOD_RATE_STATS`); the answer says "shot 45 of 126 (35.7%) on 3-pointers in the 1st quarter over 75 games", lists each game as made-attempted with its own percentage under "by game", says "attempted no free throws" where nothing was attempted rather than printing a zero, and carries the caveat or refusal of BOTH columns it divides (2002's 3-point percentage is refused with its makes; a team's rate is as weak as the weaker column's measured agreement). Not built, and each says why: a period ranking by a percentage (`period_leaderboard`: a games-played minimum says nothing about attempts, so the leader would be whoever went 3 for 3), a team's best or worst single quarter by percentage (the same, over two attempts), and TS%, eFG% and the two-point percentage (`refusals._period_stat` and `_team_period_stat` now name the three that are read). The large StatMuse feed asks this four times in 92 period questions ("jokic 4th quarter free throw shooting percentages").
- **A league-wide read honors `since`/`until`.** "players with 33 point and 13 rebound and 10 assist 2 blocks and 2 steals games since 2000-01" listed 2026's three games under a heading that said "2026 regular season", where the warehouse holds eleven regular-season games since 2001 (yardstick-v2 F161, #207): `compose.core._resolve_everyone` settled the span from `season`/`span` alone and never read the range the parser had put in the reading. It now bounds the span exactly as `scoped_player` bounds a named player's - every season from `since` on, to `until` - and declines `since` beside a named season the way `_span_of` refuses it for a player. The same read is under "nba mvps in 2010's" (#146), which now ranks 2010-2019 rather than 2026; the award is still unread.
- **`with_without` retires: the compiler answers it alone, through the team relation's `presence` group** (ROADMAP plan item 6, step (g), ninth and last template on the player relation). `Reading.group` gains `"presence"` and `TeamQuery` a `group`: a team's games inside named teammates' time on the team, each marked with how many of them held their condition (played, started, off the bench, reached a line) and the subject's line where a player is named - `compose.team._compile_team_presence` over `templates.splits._with_without_read` (the teammates, the subject and the team resolved against the box scores, the overlap of their stints, and the relation cell `conditions._with_without_games` over the team relation narrowed to the windows' teams and the opponent), said in the template's words by `_with_without_said` (`PresenceSplit` carries the read between them). The point (`compose.adapt._adapt_with_without`) carries the template's early refusals - a narrowing its words do not state (`WITH_WITHOUT_STATED`: a career, the teammates, one opponent, a companion's role), and no teammate to divide by - and a reading that gives the question up (which player was meant, a teammate with no box score, a time together outside the span) is the answer. Measured (`~/association-research/intent-shrink/g/`): 10 recorded questions, 8 identical in text and data and 2 refused both ways with the same sentence; 19 unit-test calls. `TeamResult` carries `presence`. With this, every template on the player relation but the charts is retired: `TEMPLATES` holds `fingerprint`, `player_netpoints`, `shot_chart`, `shot_distance`, the team templates, `head_to_head`, `period_leaderboard`, `team_quarter_points` and `coach`.
- **`player_matchup` retires: the compiler answers it alone, through a `pair` shape of its own** (ROADMAP plan item 6, step (g), eighth template). `Reading.shape`/`Query.skeleton` gain `"pair"`: two named players' lines over the games they met in, on opposite teams - the pair relation (`player_games.paired_rows_sql`) over the first player's games, settled and narrowed exactly as a named player's are (`compose.core._resolve_pair` through `_resolve_named`, with no window and no opponent, and the second player resolved over the same span), selecting what a meeting reads (`conditions._meetings_select`, `_meeting_rows`, `_teammate_games`, the pieces `_meetings` is now composed of). The point (`compose.adapt._adapt_player_matchup`) carries the template's early refusals - a third team, a window, an ordinal season, a quarter, then fewer or more than two names - and two names resolving to one person are refused as the pair is settled; the presenter (`compose.present._present_player_matchup`) says the meetings in the template's words (`templates.games._player_matchup_from`: the head-to-head record, each player's averages, the newest meetings, the unseen-games caveat and the absence context). Measured (`~/association-research/intent-shrink/g/`): 5 recorded questions, 3 identical in text and data and 2 refused both ways (a player in the opponent slot, named as the cause both ways); 16 unit-test calls, 13 identical and 3 refused both ways.
- **`streak` retires: the compiler answers it alone, through a `run` shape of its own** (ROADMAP plan item 6, step (g), seventh template). `Reading.shape`/`Query.skeleton` gain `"run"`: the longest runs of consecutive games the point's one predicate holds along - `(column, ">=", threshold)` for a line, `("won", "=", True|False)` for wins or losses in the games he played - read as a window over the games in Eastern-date order (`compose.core._compile_run` over the player relation, partitioned by player and keeping each player's own longest for the league-wide read; `compose.team._compile_team_run` over the team relation, partitioned by team-season, for a named team's run and the league's list with no team named). The relation cell is `conditions._longest_runs_sql`, the statement `_longest_runs` always ran, now built once and read by the compiler; a run's predicate is never a row filter (a game that misses it ends the run), its `limit` is how many runs come back, and it is read over every game in the span. The point (`compose.adapt._adapt_streak`) carries the template's early refusals - a stat with no threshold, a team's run of a stat, one date, a window or a quarter, the cells only a named player's games settle, an opponent or venue with no league-wide subject - and the presenters (`compose.present._present_streak`, `_present_team_streak`) say the runs in the template's words (`templates.splits._streak_player_answer`, `_streak_team_answer`, `_streak_league_answer`). Measured (`~/association-research/intent-shrink/g/`): 4 of 4 recorded questions identical in text and data; 41 unit-test calls, 32 identical and 9 refused both ways. `TeamResult.team` may be `None` (the league's run) and it carries `runs` and the first/last season the games came from; `Compiled.params` may be named.
- **`player_compare` retires: the compiler answers it alone** (ROADMAP plan item 6, step (g), sixth template). `compose.COMPILED_INTENTS` gains `player_compare`; the template function is gone from `TEMPLATES` and its body is the reader `templates.players._player_compare_lines(con, scope)`, which the compiler's presenter (`compose.present._present_player_compare`) calls for a pair's point on the season line (`compose.move._compare_point`: `source="seasons"`, grouped by player). The template's own refusals are the point's - fewer than two distinct names, and any narrowing at all, since it honored no scoping slot (`check_scope`'s wording kept: "player_compare cannot honor ['opponent'] - it would answer for a different span than was asked"); the reader's (an unknown or ambiguous name, a stat the line has no column for, names resolving to one person) stand as the answer's reason. Measured (`~/association-research/intent-shrink/g/`): 18 recorded questions - 16 identical in text and data, 2 refused both ways with the same sentence; the 21 unit-test calls answer through the shim.
- **`period_split` retires: the compiler answers it alone** (ROADMAP plan item 6, step (g), fifth template). `compose.COMPILED_INTENTS` gains `period_split`; the template function is gone from `TEMPLATES` and its body is the reader `templates.games._period_split_from(con, scope, player, span, narrowed, periods, period_label, measure)`, which the compiler's presenter (`compose.present._present_period_split`) calls over the player, span and period-narrowed games the compiler settled through the relation's shared steps (`compose.core.compile_query`; `_period_split_rows_from` reads the period's line off a settled narrowing, and `_period_split_rows` still narrows for the cross-season redirect). The point is `compose.adapt._adapt_period_split`: a named player's games in date order measuring the column the period's line rebuilds (points by default), the player settled over the shot table (`SHOT_AVAILABILITY`) as the template settled him; the template's early refusals are the point's own - no period, a column play-by-play cannot restrict to a period (`_period_split_measure`), a career or a `since`/`until` range (`RELATION_SCOPING_EXCLUDED["period_split"]`, the per-season accuracy caveat) - and the presenter keeps the template's order for the reconciliation refusal (`PERIOD_RECONCILIATION`, before any name is resolved; again off the game a date names). `compose.move._move_named` hands a `period_split` point to its default rather than declining a quarter or half as "the period relation's question" (a period under any other intent is still declined). `_period_split_subject` is gone with the template. Measured (`~/association-research/intent-shrink/g/`): 11 recorded questions - 10 identical in text and data, 1 refused both ways with the same sentence; the 31 unit-test calls answer through the shim.
- **`leaderboard` retires: the compiler answers it alone** (ROADMAP plan item 6, step (g), fourth template). `compose.COMPILED_INTENTS` gains `leaderboard`; the template function is gone from `TEMPLATES` and its body is the reader `templates.players._leaderboard_ranking(con, scope, position=)`, which the compiler's presenter (`compose.present._present_leaderboard`) calls for a league-wide point on the season line (`Reading.source == "seasons"`, `compose.move._leaderboard_season_line`: a stat that resolves to a leaderboard metric, no line on a column, no "at least N" floor of the question's own, no position group) - `run_leaderboard`'s pool, minimum-sample floors, traded-player dedup and the NetPoints tables, in the template's words. Where the template declined a point the game-level ranking reads at least as well (`LeaderboardStepsAside`: a stat with no season metric such as plus-minus or 3-point attempts, a position group) the presenter steps aside and that ranking answers, as it did behind the template's refusal; the template's other refusals (an unknown field, an ambiguous team, a career list with columns, a unit no metric has a form of) stand as the answer's reason. The season line's point honors `rate` (the relation's scoping check takes what the point's own reader honors); the game-level fallback refuses a stat it has no measure for by name (`move._no_ranking_for`), never ranks points in its place, and never drops a `rate` or a requested column. A leaderboard with a named player is refused in the template's words ("a leaderboard cannot answer about one named player"). Three compiler readings fixed on the way: "most triple-doubles" and "most double-doubles" are counts per player (the boolean stat's own predicate reaches the season line; the games are ranked only where the question sizes them - "highest scoring", "biggest", a stat word, or `ranked_by`), "how many 3 pointers have the magic made" is the team's own total (the template ranked the league by threes), and "with the team they play for" and "for their current team" (F017) are a column, not a team's question (`metrics.TEAM_FIELD_WORDS`, shared with the parser's field reading; `subject.kind == "team_players"` is never the team's own figure). Measured before deleting (`~/association-research/intent-shrink/g/`): over the 48 recorded questions, 41 identical, 6 the compiler answers where the template refused (plus-minus leaders, 3-point attempts, a career points list, a position group's floor named, "highest scoring triple doubles", a bare "top 5 scorers with their rebounds and assists"), 1 the team total; the template's 46 unit-test calls answer through the compiler shim, with three expectations rewritten to the improvements.
- **A question of fewer than three words is refused unread, with a generic sentence** (Jeff's rule, 2026-09-29; yardstick-v2 F112 "Tatum rec"). `refusals.too_short` answers "I couldn't understand your question, '<question>'. Please try re-phrasing it." before the normalizer is asked (`answered_by="refused"`, no model call); a recorded route is still answered as given. Short or nonsensical questions are mostly a user hitting enter early, and "Tatum rec" used to answer his splits. Measured before choosing the line (`MIN_QUESTION_WORDS = 3`): 215 of the large StatMuse feed's 2,285 questions have one or two words, almost all bare names; in the yardstick only "Tatum rec" has under three, and every three-word question ("76ers away record", "luka td3s home") answers.
- **Breaking: the tool-calling fall-through agent is gone; a question nothing reads is refused naming why.** Until now a question no template or compiled reading answered fell through to a 7B model that wrote SQL by hand. Measured at production defaults over 24 questions (ISSUES.md #129, 2026-09-18), it answered one in 23, did not finish 61% of the time and was wrong five times in six where it finished - an agent with nothing to read fills the silence from its own weights - and it slowed every test, every live run and the web page while it did. `Agent.ask` (`query/agent.py`) now answers such a question in the same second with `answered_by="refused"` and the reason the parser, the template or the compiler gave it up with (`agent.refusal_text`: "Nothing here answers this question: intent 'other' has no template yet."), which is the answer `--disable-fallthrough` used to raise as an error; `Agent.unanswered` carries the reason. A template's or the compiler's own refusal (a clarification, a "no match", a shape `query/refusals.py` names) stays `"fast"`. Gone with it: `query/prompt.py` (the preamble, the knowledge base, the tool schemas and their token budget), `query/toolbox.py` (`connect_read_only` moved to `query/connection.py`; `KNOWN_TABLES` to `nba/coverage.py`; `estimate_tokens` to `normalizer.py`), the conversation memory (`reset_conversation`, `last_question` - nothing read the previous question since 5.0.0's normalizer), `answer.FallthroughDisabled`, `models.DEFAULT_MODEL` and `AGENT_BUDGET_SECONDS`, and the CLI options `--model`, `--think`, `--no-fast-path`, `--disable-fallthrough` and `--agent-budget` on `query` and `web` (a stale script passing one is told "No such option"). `Agent(db_path, out_dir, ...)` takes the warehouse first and no model but `router_model`; `web.serve` and `web.create_app` take no `model`, and `GET /api/health` reports `models={"router": ...}` alone; `RunHistory.write` takes no `model` or `think`, and the record's header line is `router: <model>`. The page's badge says `template` or `refused`. Every docstring and comment that described the fall-through as current behavior says the refusal instead. One model is pulled (`qwen2.5:3b`); the 7B and the thinking model are not needed. Tests: the toolbox's leaderboard and shot-chart tests call `run_leaderboard` and `shotchart.render_shot_chart` directly (`tests/query/test_leaderboard.py`); the connection's disk guard is `tests/query/test_connection.py`; the agent-loop tests (SQL-as-prose recovery, thinking, trimming, the budget, the tool dispatch) are deleted with the loop. The yardstick's runners score a refusal for want of a reading as the old `fell_through` outcome, so runs before and after compare.
- **A team's quarter or half answers any stat its line holds, not only points** (the period relation's team half, ROADMAP plan item 4; ISSUES.md #161 closed). A quarter or half narrows the team-games relation (`TeamNarrowed.narrow_periods`, applied by the shared step `templates.common.team_games`; `period`/`half` join `TEAM_RELATION_SCOPING`, excluded with reasons for `team_record`, `head_to_head` and `team_leaderboard`: a quarter has no winner to count): a read sees `team_score`/`opponent_score` and `points` from ESPN's linescore, each side's own, and every other `team_games.TEAM_PERIOD_COLUMNS` column rebuilt by `team_games.team_period_line_sql` - the team's players' period lines (`player_games.period_line_sql`, each player placed by his own box row) plus the team's own plays (the turnovers charged to the team, the shots charted with no shooter). Rebounds are the players' (the box's split columns; the plays' ~6 team rebounds a game agree with nothing ESPN publishes), turnovers the team's whole count (`totalTurnovers`). `team_games.TEAM_PERIOD_AGREEMENT` holds each column's per-season agreement with `team_box_stats` over 60,422 team-games 2002-2026, and `scripts/check_team_period_lines.py` re-measures it (375/375 cells); 70 cells under 90% are refused, 60 of them 2002-2006. `team_quarter_points` answers "trailblazers stats last 10 games 3 point average 1st quarter" (F065) - "The Portland Trail Blazers averaged 4.9 3-pointers in the 1st quarter over their last 10 games" - with the season's agreement said beside a rebuilt column, refuses a season under 90% naming it, and refuses a stat nothing splits by period (minutes, plus-minus, points in the paint) by name; its points still come from the linescore, now through the relation. The compiler's team subject reads a quarter or half as a narrowing, never as the season line (`compose.team._team_narrowed`). "first-quarter" and "second-half" read as a period (`router._WHICH_QUARTER`/`_WHICH_HALF`, `parse.PARENT_GRAMMAR`): "sixers second-half assists per game" was answered with the season's `team_stat`. `refusals._team_period_stat` now refuses only a stat neither the linescore nor the line holds.
- **A period line counts a turnover or a foul its play type mislabels** (plan item 4). `player_games.period_line_sql` reads a `No Turnover` play whose text says "turnover" as one (436 of 2018's 439 plays of the type, 104 of 2019's) - but not the 23 whose text is "... no turnover ..." - a `Not Available` play whose text says "turnover" as one too (2016's 344), and a `Not Available` play whose text says "foul" as a foul (2018's 89 "personal blocking foul"s). Measured over every 2007-2026 team-game, where one missed play breaks the game: 2018 turnovers agree with the box score in 93.8% of team-games (85.4% before), 2019 95.5% (92.6%), 2022 97.5% (95.7%); 2018 fouls 83.2% (80.7%). At player level 2018 turnovers reach 99.1% and leave `PERIOD_AGREEMENT`, and 2016's rise from 93.6% to 94.5%.
- **A quarter or half used as a condition on the games is refused by name** (yardstick-v2 F062; #275). "vj edgecombe three points made per game after making one three in first quarter" is kept off the period templates by the parser (`router._PERIOD_AS_CONDITION`, plan item 4) and then fell through to the agent; `refusals._period_as_condition` names the cause - a period is the part of each game measured, and nothing keeps the games where a period held a line - and says what to ask instead.
- **`player_splits` retires: the compiler answers it alone** (ROADMAP plan item 6, step (g), third template; #228 closed). The template's tail became a reader over a settled narrowing, `templates.splits._player_splits_from(con, scope, player, narrowed, ...)`, which the compiler's presenter (`compose.present._present_player_splits`) calls over the player and games `compile_query` settled - one split or all four, in the template's own table; its team half is `templates.splits.team_splits(con, scope)`, a `grouped` point on the team relation (`compose.move.team_splits_point`) said by `present_team`. `compose.COMPILED_INTENTS` gains `player_splits`; what its words state is `STATED_SCOPING["player_splits"]` (the relation's set less a date and a window). - **A span whose years do not follow is a range, however it is written** (#261, ISSUES.md). "curry playoff stats 2015-18" answered the 2018 postseason alone, and "kobe bryant 00-02" "Kobe Bryant has no 2026 regular season numbers": `season_text.season_spans` read a four-digit span as the season it ends in and a short one only where its years follow. A span whose years do not follow is now a range - `SeasonSpan.is_range`, its `first` and `season` both season numbers, the way "2020-2024" always read: "2015-18" is 2015 through 2018, "00-02" 2000 through 2002 - and the router's range reader takes it from there (`router._validate_range_span`, in place of its own `_RANGE_HYPHEN_YEARS`, so a span has one definition); a range on one side of "to" gives that side's own end. A short range is joined by a hyphen and ascends as written: a descending pair is a line or a record ("Lebron 21-13", "the 67-15 lakers", which the century read backwards would make 1967-2015), a slash is a date or a shooting line, and a century-turning short pair ("95-02") stays unread. An ascending record now reads as a range ("celtics record 10-12" is 2010 through 2012, #168's test changed with it): of the 3,084 distinct research-corpus questions, the 4 short pairs that ascend and do not follow are all ranges and none a record, and the answer names the seasons it read. "since 2000-05" is 2000 through 2005, as "since 2000-2005" always was. `season_from_text` gives a range's last season, as it always did for four digits. Offline through the whole agent (main warehouse, the normalizer's reply stubbed), the 7 research-corpus questions with such a span: 3 now right ("kobe bryant 00-02", 212 games, 25.5 points; "Kobe bryant 00-03"; "Vince carter stats 00-02"), 2 ask which Curry or Love (a range does not narrow a name - the four-digit forms ask the same; filed), 2 fall through where a template takes no range (`with_without`, `team_stat`, as their four-digit forms do). Rehearsal (628, no model) and goldens v1 (631) and v2 (628): nothing moves.

- **A holiday is its own day, and every holiday the calendar reads is one the router captures** (#238, ISSUES.md). "on mlk day" matched every January 15, which is MLK Day in 5 of the 33 seasons 1994-2026: "lebron stats on mlk day" answered his January 15 game (29 points against Charlotte) as MLK Day, where MLK Day 2026 was January 19 and the Lakers did not play. It is the third Monday of January now - a new `CalendarNarrowing` kind, `"nth_weekday"`, read from each game's own Eastern date (the nth of a weekday falls on days 7n-6 to 7n of its month, so no calendar is computed per season), checked day by day for 1988-2040 against the published MLK Days and against the ISSUES entry's own `make_date` expression. The router's holiday words are built from the calendar's own list (`calendar.HOLIDAY_WORDS`, longest spelling first), so the two cannot drift again: "valentine's day", a day the calendar read that the router's hand-kept list never captured, narrowed nothing and answered the season line; "christmas eve" and "new year's eve", captured as "christmas" and "new year's", answered the day after. Each is its own day now, and "new years day", "new years" and "martin luther king day" are read where they were refused. Thanksgiving, the fourth Thursday of November, is read too - it was refused only because no moving date could be stated; Easter is still captured and refused by name (`calendar.UNREAD_HOLIDAYS`). Everything downstream of the Reading reads typed fields: the relation's scoping check, the starter/bench and window rules, a team beside a player, the team subject's season-line-or-games split and its coverage floor, the moves the question's words make, the default-point adapters (`to_reading` and `to_query` still take a slot dict, through `Scope.from_slots`) and the presenters (`compose.present.present` takes the Query alone). The router's slot dict is edited only before its scope is read (`move.repair` and the position, filler and team repairs); the templates' shared steps and helpers are handed `scope.to_slots()` until they take the Scope. Golden 631/631 identical over the routing corpus and the day10 routes; the parser's offline rehearsal moves nothing.
- **The shared scoping steps read the typed Scope** (ROADMAP plan item 6, step (d)). `check_scope`, `check_coverage`, `coverage_caveat`, `scoped_player`, `scoped_games`, `league_games`, `condition_player`, `scoped_team` and `team_games` in `templates.common` - and the small readers beside them (`_slot_season`, `_player_relation_season_type`, `_relation_window`, the coverage floors' table choice) - read `reading.Scope`'s fields rather than a slot dict, and a `conditions` entry as a `ConditionSpec`. Each takes a `Scope` or, until every caller passes `reading.scope`, the slot dict, typed on the way in by `Scope.from_slots`: a value nothing types is refused there, as it already was where the agent builds the Reading. `condition_player`'s own `_Scope` parameter is `condition_scope` now, and it takes `opponent=` - a team the caller already resolved, which a Scope (it holds names) cannot carry; `player_splits`' slot dict still carries it as the Entity. Behavior-identical: the golden replay of the routing corpus and the day10 routes is 631/631 byte-identical, and the parser's offline rehearsal moves no answer.
- **Every template takes the Reading** (ROADMAP plan item 6, step (d)). A template is now `template(ctx, reading)`, and the agent hands each one `Reading.from_slots(...)` of the settled route; the bodies still read the slot dict (`reading.scope.to_slots()`) until each module reads the typed scope directly. `conditions` is typed too (`reading.ConditionSpec`: player, side, predicate, and a reached line), and a bare string in a name or phrase list is one item, as `teammate_names` always read it. Values nothing could answer - a span of "decade", a side of "sideways", a shot value of 0, a condition predicate the relation does not read - are refused where the Reading is built rather than ignored or refused by one template.
- **The Reading is typed** (ROADMAP plan item 6, step (d), first part). `reading.Scope` holds the scoping as one typed field per slot - frozen, keyword-only, `Literal` where the values are a closed set (a season type is 2 or 3, a venue home or away, an order recent or first) - and `Reading` is frozen and keyword-only with `Literal` shapes, aggregates, groups and relations, so mypy and pyright hold every construction to them: the switch turned up five places passing a plain string where a closed set is meant. `Scope.from_slots` is the one door a slot dict comes in by and raises on a key or value it does not type, rather than dropping a narrowing (every one of the 1,185 recorded routes passes it and round-trips exactly through `Scope.to_slots`, which the templates and the compiler read until they read the Reading).
- **A swapped pair of letters is one edit when the question is checked for a name** (ISSUES #239). `subject.question_supports` measured near spellings with a hand-written plain Levenshtein, which charges a transposition twice, while the entity index measures Damerau-Levenshtein in DuckDB - so "jokci stats" did not support the router's Nikola Jokic that the index would have read, and the answer was the misread-name refusal ("... who the question does not mention"). The check now uses rapidfuzz's `DamerauLevenshtein` (a new core dependency, MIT, typed, no dependencies of its own): proven equal to the old function's metric on 142,880 real word pairs before the switch, and to DuckDB's on every ASCII pair.
- **A count spelled out is the count** (ROADMAP plan item 6, step (c)). The parser's number words are one table, one to ninety-nine and a hundred (hyphen and space forms), and every count pattern it reads is built from it: "jrue holiday last twelve games" read as his season line, and "celtics record last eleven games" as the season record, while the digits read the log.
- **Changed: the parser reads the question** (ROADMAP plan item 6, steps (c)-(d)). `Agent`, `association query` and `association web` read every question with the parser, where the router's model classified it: the model copies the names and picks a stat, and `parse.read_route` reads the rest (the entry on `router.route` says what went with the router's classification). Measured on yardstick-v2's live runs over the same 277 wordings: 162/175 primary questions and 151/166 families against the router's 160 and 150, 3 wrong answers against 4, at 1.08s a question median against 2.28s (5.3 minutes for the run against 11.3). A name the model corrected is put back as the question typed it (`parse._as_typed`): "how many points does embid average" came back from the model as "embiid" and was answered about Joel Embiid with nothing saying a typo was read; the typo now reaches the entity index, which reads it visibly.
- **The parser's tables, held against questions nothing was tuned on** (ROADMAP plan item 6, step (c)). The recorded routing corpus's 75 questions outside day10, answered by the parser and by their recorded routes, turned up six the parser alone got wrong: a "%" after a space ("3pt %") read as 3-pointers made (the pattern's `\b%` could never match), a team's "opening game" as its season line, a team's "playoff odds" as its postseason stats, "worst record 2025-26" as the league's scorers, and attempts asked beside a misspelled "made" as the attempted column, which has no per-game line (`router._route_attempted_stat` reads "mad" as made now). The columns a ranking asks to see are read from the words - "with their rebounds and assists", "the team they play for" - as the leaderboard's `fields`, which the router's model used to fill (yardstick-v2 F017, answered with the rows and the teams asked for).
- **Three wrong answers the parser's live run exposed, fixed on both paths** (ROADMAP plan item 6, step (c)). A "since" written in numbers is read: "since 1/26/20" narrows to every game from that calendar date on (`calendar.CalendarNarrowing` kind `since_date`, one cut across seasons, parsed with `time.strptime`), and its year starts the seasons read, where the date used to be dropped silently and "towns home rec including playoffs since 1/26/20 vs spurs" answered his whole career (yardstick-v2 F110); "since 1/26" with no year is the day-of-the-season reading "since January 26" already had. Only after a range word, so a shooting line ("7/14") is never a date. A team metric the question qualifies as given up is named as asked ("rebounds allowed"), so the template refuses by name where it ranked the teams' own rebounds (F101). And "rec" is a player's record, read before a date or window can make it a log.
- **The parser reads the question in place of the router** (ROADMAP plan item 6, step (c)). `query/normalizer.py` is the model's whole remaining job: copy the names out of the question exactly as typed and pick one stat key, under a two-field schema (`NORMALIZER_PROMPT`, `NORMALIZER_SCHEMA`, `normalize()`). The agent sends the question through it and `parse.read_route()`, which reads the intent and every other slot from the words, and then down the router's path unchanged. `read_route` is the first half of `parse()` split out: the route in the router's own shape, before the compiler's repairs. It writes the name slots from the subject reading rather than the model's spans (a name the model dropped that the question holds is read; a companion is never a second player; a team beside a player is his opponent), reads a team's code as the team ("PHI" is also inside a player's name), reads the window before the stages so a bare "last 10 games" reads both season types as a routed one does, and reads a team's quarter from the words. A conference word ("vs west" - four Wests played) and an indefinite pronoun ("someone" is one near spelling from Simone Fontecchio) are never a name span, and a companion is taken out of the player slots even when the model named nobody else. "alltime" written as one word is a career span (`router._SPAN_WORDS` needed the hyphen or the space): read by the parser, "alperen şengün alltime record" (yardstick-v2 F111) answered his 2026 season alone. Rehearsed over the 277 day10 wordings with the normalizer's recorded replies and no model at all: 263 answered against the live run's 272, the gap being rows the grammar and the index still owe (#231's record rows, typos). Also: every `versionadded`/`versionchanged` this cycle wrote as 4.6.0 now says 5.0.0, the release they ship in.
- **A single near spelling is that player, said in the answer** (ROADMAP plan item 6, step (c): typos are the entity index's job, never the model's). A name slot that matches nobody exactly but is within the edit budget of exactly one player - every word of it - resolves to him instead of asking "did you mean": "How many times has webanyama fouled out of a game" answers Victor Wembanyama's 3 games, ending "('webanyama' matches no player exactly and was read as Victor Wembanyama, the only near spelling on record - spell the name exactly to ask about someone else.)". New `entities.read_near_spelling`, called by `resolve_player` and by `shotchart.resolve_chart_player`; the agent's chart tools (`render_shot_chart`, `render_fingerprint`) append the sentence themselves, since nothing above them collects it. Two or more near spellings still ask, a team's name is still nobody, and the surname back-off ("Jemel Embiid", "Larry Bird") still asks - now in `without` too, which used to take a lone back-off survivor. `note_typo_reading`'s sentence now says how to reach anyone else. Measured on the warehouse: of 10,602 one-letter drops, doubles and swaps of the 591 2026 players' surnames, 3,597 default (every one to the player misspelled) and 2,731 still ask; the golden corpus moves on 3 of 631 rows, each the webanyama answer or the new sentence. A possessive typed without its apostrophe is read the same way where the spelling as typed is near nobody: "joel embids fingerprint" is Joel Embiid (two edits, one of them the "s"), as the parser's `classify_span` already read it.
- **The parser's tables, second pass: the held-out paraphrases** (ROADMAP plan item 6, step (b)). In `query/parse.py`: a player's own record reads `player_splits` - his games' W-L - never the team's with/without split (F088, "Embiid's record against Boston this year"; ISSUES #231 on the parser path; a line in it, "Sga record 36 plus points", stays `record_when`); a team's triple-doubles are its players' (`leaderboard`); "plot" and the shots in either order are a shot chart; "his most recent game" is a game log; "compared to other teams" is an outlook; two teams meeting with a record asked for stay two teams under a window ("lakers vs mavs record last 10 home games"). `MEASURE_GRAMMAR` reads a three as its own column ("3 point stats", "three points made" were points) and what a team gives up as the opponent's line ("rebounds allowed per team" was answered with the teams' own rebounds; it now names a key no template ranks and refuses - ISSUES has the gap), and no longer reads the word "to" as turnovers. `WINDOW_GRAMMAR` reads "final two regular season games", "last 10 home games" and a closing "last 10", and no longer sets a limit of 1 on "who led the league in ..." - the ranking already leads with the one and names the runners-up. Live, in `subject.py`'s child grammars and the router's text readers (0 false positives over the recorded corpus, golden 631/631): a line written "36-plus", "30-point" or "at least 2" is a line; "in one match" is one game and "per game" never is ("the highest points per game average" read `single_game_high`); "from year to year" is a history; "excluding" is "without" and "featuring" is "with"; a question word ends a companion phrase, so a fronted "Without Kevin Durant, what is Steph Curry's record" no longer reads Curry as absent. `threshold_count` counts on its one line's own column where the stat beside it keeps no threshold ("Sga games with under 14 fta" with `freeThrowsAttempted` refused).
- **The parser, first tables** (ROADMAP plan item 6, step (b)). `query/parse.py` reads a question into one `Reading` with no router: the model's contribution arrives as data (the names it copied, the stat key it chose - `parse(con, question, names, stat)`), every span is classified by the entity index before it can be a subject (a division, the word "team" or a two-way typo is nobody's; a single near spelling is that player - the typo policy), and the kind and parent intent come from `PARENT_GRAMMAR` (rows keyed on the subject kind, `with_without` only beside a companion the reading found), the window from `WINDOW_GRAMMAR` ("last 10 games", "his last game", "top 5", "who led the league in"), the stat from `MEASURE_GRAMMAR` (the NetPoints family, differentials, plus-minus, the rates) before the model's key; the scope, the children and the point come from the readers the pipeline already has (`read_subject`, `settle`, `read_point`). The child grammars for `threshold_count` and `record_when` gain the paraphrases' shapes ("which games had 15 or more assists", "the highest number of 30+ point games", "36 plus points sga record"); 0 false positives over 263 recorded rows of other intents. - **The Reading: one record of what a question asks, in front of the compiler** (ROADMAP plan item 6, step (a)). `query/reading.py` holds `Reading` - the relation, the subject, the shape, the measures, the predicates, the window, the scope, the source - and `compose/plan.py` turns one into the compiler's point (`Query` or `TeamQuery`) without reading the question: the compiler's own word reading (`move.read_point`, the adapters' `to_reading`) now builds a `Reading`, and `move_point`/`to_query`/`team_move_point` are the reading planned. `compose.answer` takes a `trace` callback the agent uses to log the record as `-> (reading) ...`, the line that says where every value in a composed answer came from. Measured over the recorded corpus (`~/association-research/intent-shrink/parity.py`, text and `data` both identical to the template on the same slots): `threshold_count` 18/18 (was 1), `single_game_high` 10/10 (was 1), `record_when` 10/10 (was 0), `game_log` 19/26 (was 2; all 19 player logs, none of the 7 team logs), `player_stat` 6/29 (was 0; the 6 narrowed reads - the other 23 read the season line); `player_history` (season lines) and `player_splits` stay 0. Fixed on the way, in the compiler: a per-game usage rate printed as "2435.5%" (#222 - `usage_pct` is stored as a percent, not a fraction); a composed answer carried the partial-season caveat twice (the agent appends it; `compose.answer` and `run_team` appended it too, and `TeamResult.coverage_note` is gone); "past 4 seasons" of a player's history listed his FIRST four (ordered by the label ascending, now newest first and headed "most recent N seasons"); a `single_game_high` question without "in a game" ranked per-game averages ("what was the highest scoring game this year" named Luka Doncic's 33.5 average, not Bam Adebayo's 83); "most games with 15+ assists" declined for want of a line (the router's own stat at its threshold is the line); "who had the most 30+ point 10+ rebound games" listed games instead of counting them by player; a log or top-games read never showed a rebuilt game (`minutes` is exempt from the rebuilt-line rule, as it is for `game_log`); `own_team` ("lebron stats as a starter for Miami") was ignored, averaging 1,612 career starts where the template counts his 294 for Miami; `season_type_unstated` ("including the playoffs") is honored for a named player instead of declining; "how many times has embiid fouled out" reads as `fouls >= 6`, the router's own line; and a player the reading placed beside a team subject ("stats for sixers when maxey scored 20+") is no longer moved into `team` and resolved as a team called "Maxey". Golden over the 308 recorded questions: 307 identical, the one move being `player_history`'s newest-first order.
